title.zh: 卷一百八十六 列傳第一百十一 周王鄧陳齊趙二楊顧
title.en: Volume 186 Biographies 111: Zhou, Wang, Deng, Cheng, Qi, Zhao, two Yangs, Gu
title.raw: 卷一百八十六 列傳第一百十一 周王鄧陳齊趙二楊顧 Volume 186 Biographies 111: Zhou, Wang, Deng, Cheng, Qi, Zhao, two Yangs, Gu

sentences.zh: 周王鄧陳齊趙二楊顧

translations.literal: Zhou, Wang, Deng, Cheng, Qi, Zhao, the two Yangs, and Gu
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Zhou, Wang, Deng, Cheng, Qi, Zhao, the two men surnamed Yang, and Gu

sentences.zh: 周寶，字上珪，平州盧龍人。

translations.literal: Zhou Bao, courtesy name Shanggui, was a native of Lulong in Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bao, whose courtesy name was Shanggui, came from Lulong in Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖待選，為魯城令，安祿山反，率縣人拒戰，死之。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Daixuan served as magistrate of Lucheng; when An Lushan rebelled, he led the county people to resist in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Daixuan had been magistrate of Lucheng; when An Lushan rose in revolt, he rallied the county to resist and was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 祖光濟，事平盧節度希逸為牙將，每戰，得攻魯城者，必手屠之。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guangji served the Pinglu governor Li Xiyi as a yaji general; in every battle, whoever captured Lucheng, he would personally slaughter them.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guangji was a yaji officer under Li Xiyi, military governor of Pinglu; after every battle, he personally killed any soldier who had taken Lucheng.

sentences.zh: 歷左贊善大夫，從李洧以徐州歸天子。

translations.literal: He rose through the office of Left Remonstrance Counselor and followed Li Si in surrendering Xuzhou to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually held the post of Left Remonstrance Counselor and followed Li Si when Xuzhou was surrendered to the throne.

sentences.zh: 父懷義，通書記，擢累檢校工部尚書、天德西城防禦使，以徙城事不為宰相李吉甫所助，以憂死。

translations.literal: His father Huaiyi was skilled at secretarial work, was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of Works and Defender of the Western Sector of Tiande, and died from grief because the relocation of the city was not assisted by Chancellor Li Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaiyi was adept at secretarial duties and rose to Acting Minister of Works and Defender of the Western Sector of Tiande, but died of grief when Chancellor Li Jifu refused to support the plan to relocate the city.

sentences.zh: 寶藉蔭為千牛備身。

translations.literal: Bao entered office by yin privilege as a Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Bao entered service through hereditary privilege as a Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.

sentences.zh: 天平節度使殷侑嘗為懷義參軍，寶從之，為部將。

translations.literal: Yin You, military governor of Tianping, had once served as Huaiyi's aide; Bao followed him and became a subordinate officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You, governor of Tianping, had once been Huaiyi's staff officer; Bao followed him and served as a company commander.

sentences.zh: 會昌時，選方鎮才校入宿衛，與高駢皆隸右神策軍，歷良原鎮使，以善擊球，俱備軍將，駢以兄事寶。

translations.literal: During Huichang, talented officers from frontier commands were selected for palace guard duty; he and Gao Pian both served in the Right Shence Army, became garrison commanders at Liangyuan, and for skill at cuju ball both held preparedness general posts; Pian treated Bao as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang era, able officers from the provinces were drafted into the capital guard; he and Gao Pian both joined the Right Shence Army and served as garrison commanders at Liangyuan. Their skill at cuju won them both posts as preparedness generals, and Pian treated Bao as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 寶強毅，未嘗詘意於人。

translations.literal: Bao was strong-willed and never bent his will to others.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was resolute by nature and never humbled himself before anyone.

sentences.zh: 官不進，自請以球見，武宗稱其能，擢金吾將軍。

translations.literal: His rank did not advance; he requested an audience through cuju ball; Wuzong praised his ability and promoted him to Golden Crow general.
translations.idiomatic: When his promotion stalled, he asked to demonstrate his cuju skill before the throne; Wuzong praised his talent and made him a Golden Crow general.

sentences.zh: 以球喪一目。

translations.literal: In playing ball he lost an eye.
translations.idiomatic: He lost an eye in a cuju match.

sentences.zh: 進檢校工部尚書、涇原節度使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Minister of Works and military governor of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Minister of Works and military governor of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 務耕力，聚糧二十萬斛，號良將。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to farming and labor, amassed two hundred thousand hu of grain, and was called a capable general.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed farming and corvée labor, stockpiled two hundred thousand hu of grain, and was acclaimed as an able commander.

sentences.zh: 黃巢據宣、歙，徙寶鎮海軍節度兼南面招討使。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao held Xuancheng and She Prefectures, Bao was transferred to military governor of Zhenhai Army with concurrent southern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao seized Xuancheng and Shezhou, Bao was reassigned as military governor of the Zhenhai Army with the additional title of southern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 巢聞，出采石，略揚州。

translations.literal: Chao heard of this and withdrew to Caishi, raided Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao heard the news, he withdrew to Caishi and raided Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗入蜀，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong entered Sichuan, Bao was given the additional title of Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xizong fled into Sichuan, Bao was given the additional rank of Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 時群盜所在盤結，柳超據常熟，王敖據昆山，王騰據華亭，宋可復據無錫。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were entrenched everywhere: Liu Chao held Changshu, Wang Ao Kunshan, Wang Teng Huating, and Song Kefu Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits had dug in across the region: Liu Chao held Changshu, Wang Ao Kunshan, Wang Teng Huating, and Song Kefu Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 寶練卒自守，發杭州兵戍縣鎮，判八都：石鏡都，董昌主之；

translations.literal: Bao drilled troops to defend himself, sent Hangzhou soldiers to garrison county towns, and divided eight commands: the Shijing Command under Dong Chang;
translations.idiomatic: Bao trained troops for self-defense, dispatched Hangzhou forces to garrison the counties, and organized eight commands: the Shijing Command under Dong Chang;

sentences.zh: 清平都，陳晟主之；

translations.literal: the Qingping Command under Chen Sheng;
translations.idiomatic: the Qingping Command under Chen Sheng;

sentences.zh: 於潛都，吳文舉主之；

translations.literal: the Yuqian Command under Wu Wenju;
translations.idiomatic: the Yuqian Command under Wu Wenju;

sentences.zh: 鹽官都，徐及主之；

translations.literal: the Yanguan Command under Xu Ji;
translations.idiomatic: the Yanguan Command under Xu Ji;

sentences.zh: 新登都，杜棱主之；

translations.literal: the Xindeng Command under Du Ling;
translations.idiomatic: the Xindeng Command under Du Ling;

sentences.zh: 唐山都，饒京主之；

translations.literal: the Tangshan Command under Rao Jing;
translations.idiomatic: the Tangshan Command under Rao Jing;

sentences.zh: 富春都，文禹主之；

translations.literal: the Fuchun Command under Wen Yu;
translations.idiomatic: the Fuchun Command under Wen Yu;

sentences.zh: 龍泉都，淩文舉主之。

translations.literal: and the Longquan Command under Ling Wenju.
translations.idiomatic: and the Longquan Command under Ling Wenju.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，進同中書門上平章事，兼天下租庸副使，封汝南郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe he was advanced to Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery with concurrent deputy commissioner for empire-wide land tax and corvée, and enfeoffed as Prince of Runan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe he was made Grand Councilor and deputy commissioner for empire-wide land tax and corvée, and enfeoffed as Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 寶和裕，喜接士，以京師陷賊，將赴難，益募兵，號「後樓都」。

translations.literal: Bao was mild and generous, delighted in receiving scholars; because the capital had fallen to bandits, he prepared to go to the rescue and further recruited troops, calling them the "Rear Pavilion Command."
translations.idiomatic: Bao was easygoing and fond of entertaining men of letters; when the capital fell to rebels he prepared to march to its relief, raised more troops, and styled them the "Rear Pavilion Command."

sentences.zh: 明年，董昌據杭州，柳超自常熟入睦州，刺史韋諸殺之。

translations.literal: The next year Dong Chang seized Hangzhou; Liu Chao advanced from Changshu into Muzhou, and the prefect Wei Zhu killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Dong Chang seized Hangzhou; Liu Chao marched from Changshu into Muzhou, where Prefect Wei Zhu killed him.

sentences.zh: 四年，餘杭鎮使陳晟攻諸，諸以州授晟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Yuhang garrison commander Chen Sheng attacked Zhu, and Zhu surrendered the prefecture to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Chen Sheng, garrison commander of Yuhang, attacked Zhu, who surrendered the prefecture to him.

sentences.zh: 寶子玙統後樓都，孱不能馭軍，部伍橫肆。

translations.literal: Bao's son Yu commanded the Rear Pavilion Command but was weak and could not control the army; the ranks ran wild.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son Yu took command of the Rear Pavilion troops, but he was too weak to discipline them and the ranks ran riot.

sentences.zh: 寶亦稍惑色，不恤事，以婿楊茂實為蘇州刺史，重斂，人不聊。

translations.literal: Bao himself gradually became infatuated with women and neglected affairs; he made his son-in-law Yang Maoshi prefect of Suzhou, who levied heavy taxes until the people could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Bao himself grew distracted by pleasure and neglected government; he installed his son-in-law Yang Maoshi as prefect of Suzhou, whose crushing levies left the people desperate.

sentences.zh: 田令孜以趙載代之，茂實不受命。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi sent Zhao Zai to replace him, but Maoshi refused the order.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi appointed Zhao Zai to replace him, but Maoshi refused to step down.

sentences.zh: 寶表留，不聽，乃殘郛署、汙垣牖去。

translations.literal: Bao memorialized to retain him but was not heeded; Maoshi then ravaged the outer offices, defiled the walls and windows, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Bao petitioned to keep him in office but was overruled; Maoshi then wrecked the government compound, defaced the buildings, and departed.

sentences.zh: 詔以王蘊代載，載留潤州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wang Yun to replace Zai, but Zai remained at Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wang Yun to replace Zhao Zai, but Zai stayed on at Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，鎮海將張郁以擊球事寶。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Zhenhai general Zhang Yu had served Bao through cuju ball.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Zhenhai officer Zhang Yu had entered Bao's service through their shared passion for cuju.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，劇賊剽昆山，寶遣郁領兵三百戍海上，郁醉而叛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, fierce bandits raided Kunshan; Bao sent Yu with three hundred troops to garrison the coast, but Yu got drunk and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangqi era, fierce raiders pillaged Kunshan; Bao sent Yu with three hundred men to guard the coast, but Yu got drunk and mutinied.

sentences.zh: 王蘊謂州兵還休，不設備，郁遂大掠，蘊嬰城守。

translations.literal: Wang Yun thought the prefectural troops had returned for rest and made no preparations; Yu then plundered on a large scale, and Yun shut himself in the city to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun assumed the prefectural troops had gone off duty and took no precautions; Yu looted the city wholesale, forcing Yun to bar the gates and hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 寶遣將拓拔從討定之。

translations.literal: Bao sent the general Tuo Ba Cong to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao dispatched the general Tuo Ba Cong to put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 郁保常熟，因攻常州，刺史劉革迎降，眾稍集。

translations.literal: Yu held Changshu, then attacked Changzhou; the prefect Liu Ge welcomed him in surrender, and his following gradually gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Yu held Changshu, then turned on Changzhou; Prefect Liu Ge surrendered to him, and his forces steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 寶遣將丁從實督兵攻之，郁走海陵，依鎮遏使高霸，從實遂據常州。

translations.literal: Bao sent the general Ding Congshi to lead troops against him; Yu fled to Hailing and relied on the suppression commissioner Gao Ba, while Congshi then seized Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sent Ding Congshi to attack him; Yu fled to Hailing under the protection of suppression commissioner Gao Ba, and Congshi seized Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 及董昌徙義勝軍節度使，寶承制擢杭州都將錢镠領州事。

translations.literal: When Dong Chang was transferred to military governor of Yisheng Army, Bao by imperial order promoted Hangzhou commander Qian Liu to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Chang was reassigned as governor of the Yisheng Army, Bao appointed Hangzhou commander Qian Liu to govern the prefecture by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 宣州賊李君旺陷義興守之。

translations.literal: The Xuancheng bandit Li Junwang seized Yixing and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Junwang, a rebel from Xuancheng, captured Yixing and held it.

sentences.zh: 是時，右散騎常侍沈誥使至江南，負田令孜勢，震暴州縣。

translations.literal: At this time the Right Regular Attendant Shen Gao arrived in Jiangnan as envoy, relying on Tian Lingzi's power and terrifying the prefectures and counties with violence.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Shen Gao, Right Regular Attendant, arrived in the south as an imperial envoy; backed by Tian Lingzi's power, he terrorized the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王下令搜令孜黨，寶收誥及趙載殺之。

translations.literal: The heir of Prince Xiang of Xiang ordered a search for Tian Lingzi's faction; Bao arrested Gao and Zhao Zai and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The heir of Prince Xiang ordered a purge of Tian Lingzi's partisans; Bao arrested Shen Gao and Zhao Zai and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 高駢領鹽鐵，辟寶子佶為支使，寶亦表駢從子在幕府。

translations.literal: Gao Pian headed the Salt and Iron Commission and recruited Bao's son Ji as disbursement commissioner; Bao also memorialized to place Pian's nephew in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian headed the Salt and Iron Commission and took Bao's son Ji as disbursement commissioner; Bao in turn placed Pian's nephew on his own staff.

sentences.zh: 駢為都統，浸不禮寶，寶銜之。

translations.literal: When Pian became supreme commander, he gradually ceased to treat Bao with courtesy, and Bao harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pian became supreme commander, he grew increasingly dismissive of Bao, who nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 帝在蜀，淮南絕貢賦，謾言道浙西為寶剽阻。

translations.literal: The emperor was in Sichuan; Huainan cut off tribute and taxes, falsely claiming that Zhexi was plundered and blocked by Bao.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor in Sichuan, Huainan stopped sending tribute, spreading the lie that Bao was raiding and blocking the Zhexi route.

sentences.zh: 帝知其誣，不直駢，自是顯隙。

translations.literal: The emperor knew it was slander and did not side with Pian; from then on their rift was open.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through the slander and refused to take Pian's side, and from then on their breach was plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 駢出屯東塘，約西定京師，寶喜，將赴之，或曰：「高氏欲圖公地。」

translations.literal: Pian moved out to garrison Dongtang, proposing to pacify the west and restore the capital; Bao was delighted and prepared to go, but someone said, "The Gao clan intends to seize your territory.
translations.idiomatic: Pian encamped at Dongtang, pledging to secure the west and restore the capital; Bao was elated and prepared to march, until someone warned him, "The Gao family means to seize your territory.

sentences.zh: 寶未信。

translations.literal: Bao did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Bao refused to believe it.

sentences.zh: 駢遣人請會金山，謀執寶，寶答曰：「平時且不聞境上會，況上蒙塵，宗廟焚辱，寧高會時耶？

translations.literal: Pian sent someone to invite a meeting at Jinshan, planning to seize Bao; Bao replied, "In ordinary times one never heard of meetings on the border—how much less now, when the sovereign suffers disgrace and the ancestral temples are burned and shamed? Would this be a time for Gao to meet?
translations.idiomatic: Pian sent envoys inviting him to a meeting at Jinshan, intending to seize him; Bao replied, "Even in peacetime we never met on the border—how can Gao propose a conference now, when the Son of Heaven is in exile and the ancestral temples lie in ashes? Is this a time for celebration?

sentences.zh: 我非李康，不能為人作功勛、欺朝廷也。」

translations.literal: I am not Li Kang—I cannot earn merit for another man and deceive the court.
translations.idiomatic: I am no Li Kang; I will not win another man's glory by deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 駢遣人切讓，寶亦詬絕之。

translations.literal: Pian sent someone to rebuke him sharply; Bao also reviled and cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: Pian sent a stern rebuke; Bao answered with curses and broke off relations.

sentences.zh: 會部將劉浩、刁頵與度支催勘使、太子左庶子薛朗叛，寶方寢，外兵格鬥，火照城中。

translations.literal: Then the subordinate generals Liu Hao and Diao Yun rebelled together with the revenue audit commissioner and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent Xue Lang; Bao was just asleep when outer troops fought, fire lighting the city.
translations.idiomatic: Then his officers Liu Hao and Diao Yun joined Revenue Audit Commissioner and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent Xue Lang in revolt; Bao was still asleep when fighting broke out beyond the walls and flames lit up the city.

sentences.zh: 寶驚出，諭曰：「為吾用則吾兵，否則寇也。

translations.literal: Bao rushed out in alarm and addressed them: "Serve me and you are my soldiers; otherwise you are bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rushed out and shouted, "Fight for me and you are my men; fight against me and you are nothing but rebels.

sentences.zh: 六州皆我鎮，何往不適？」

translations.literal: All six prefectures are my command—where can you not go?
translations.idiomatic: All six prefectures belong to my command—where can you not find a home?

sentences.zh: 乃自青陽門出奔。

translations.literal: He then fled out through the Qingyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled through the Qingyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 士大掠，官屬崔綰、陸鍔、田倍皆死。

translations.literal: The soldiers plundered on a great scale; the officials Cui Wan, Lu E, and Tian Bei all died.
translations.idiomatic: The troops looted the city; officials Cui Wan, Lu E, and Tian Bei were all killed.

sentences.zh: 浩奉朗領府事。

translations.literal: Hao installed Lang to head prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hao installed Xue Lang as head of the prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 寶至奔牛埭，駢饋以葛，諷其且亡也。

translations.literal: When Bao reached Benniu Ford, Pian sent him hemp cloth, insinuating that he was about to perish.
translations.idiomatic: At Benniu Ford, Pian sent him a gift of hemp cloth—a pointed hint that his end was near.

sentences.zh: 寶抵於地曰：「公有呂用之，難方作，無誚我！」

translations.literal: Bao struck it to the ground and said, "You have your Lu Yongzhi—trouble is just beginning; do not mock me!
translations.idiomatic: Bao dashed it to the ground and cried, "You have your own Lu Yongzhi—your troubles are only beginning; spare me your mockery!

sentences.zh: 即奔常州依丁從實，召後樓都，無一士至者。

translations.literal: He then fled to Changzhou to rely on Ding Congshi, summoned the Rear Pavilion Command, but not a single soldier came.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Changzhou to seek refuge with Ding Congshi and called up the Rear Pavilion troops, but not one man answered.

sentences.zh: 錢镠遣杜棱、成及攻薛朗，棱子建徽攻從實，聲言迎寶，擊破賊君旺，取船八百艘，遂圍常州，從實奔海陵。

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent Du Ling and Cheng Ji to attack Xue Lang; Ling's son Jianhui attacked Congshi, claiming to welcome Bao; they defeated the bandit Junwang, took eight hundred boats, then besieged Changzhou, and Congshi fled to Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent Du Ling and Cheng Ji against Xue Lang; Ling's son Jianhui attacked Congshi under the pretext of welcoming Bao back, routed the rebel Li Junwang, seized eight hundred vessels, and besieged Changzhou until Congshi fled to Hailing.

sentences.zh: 镠具橐迎寶，舍樟亭。

translations.literal: Liu prepared a welcome with full equipage and lodged Bao at Zhangting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu went out with full honors to receive Bao and lodged him at Zhangting.

sentences.zh: 未幾，殺之，不淹月，而駢為畢師鐸所囚。

translations.literal: Before long he killed him; within less than a month Pian was imprisoned by Bi Shiduo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he had Bao killed; within the month Gao Pian himself was taken prisoner by Bi Shiduo.

sentences.zh: 寶死，年七十四，贈太保。

translations.literal: Bao died at seventy-four; he was posthumously given Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Bao died at the age of seventy-four and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 镠以杜棱守常州。

translations.literal: Liu appointed Du Ling to defend Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu placed Du Ling in command of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 文德元年拔潤州，劉浩亡，不知所在，執朗，剖其心祭寶，使阮結守潤州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wende he captured Runzhou; Liu Hao fled, his whereabouts unknown; he seized Lang, cut out his heart to sacrifice to Bao, and sent Ruan Jie to defend Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wende he took Runzhou; Liu Hao vanished without trace; he captured Xue Lang, cut out his heart as an offering to Bao's spirit, and left Ruan Jie to hold Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊行密殺高霸，而張郁、丁從實皆死。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi killed Gao Ba, and Zhang Yu and Ding Congshi both died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi killed Gao Ba; Zhang Yu and Ding Congshi also met their deaths.

sentences.zh: 初，黃巢平，時溥遣小史李師悅上符璽，拜湖州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huang Chao was pacified, Shi Pu sent the minor clerk Li Shiyue to present the imperial seals and was appointed prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Huang Chao's defeat, Shi Pu sent his clerk Li Shiyue to present the imperial seals to the throne, and Li was appointed prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭宗時，遷忠國軍節度使。

translations.literal: During Emperor Zhaozong's reign he was transferred to military governor of Zhongguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he was made military governor of the Zhongguo Army.

sentences.zh: 董昌反，師悅連和，與镠有隙，而結好於行密，安仁義次潤州，復助之。

translations.literal: When Dong Chang rebelled, Shiyue allied with him, had a rift with Liu, but formed good relations with Xingmi; An Renyi was stationed at Runzhou and again assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Chang rebelled, Shiyue joined him, fell out with Qian Liu, but cultivated ties with Yang Xingmi; An Renyi, encamped at Runzhou, aided him as well.

sentences.zh: 乾寧三年卒，子繼徽代，以地附行密，其將沈攸謂不可，繼徽乃奔揚州。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Qianning; his son Jihui succeeded him, attached his territory to Xingmi, but his general Shen You said it could not be done, and Jihui then fled to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Qianning; his son Jihui succeeded him and offered the territory to Yang Xingmi, but his general Shen You objected, and Jihui fled to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王處存，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun came from Wannian in the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 世籍神策軍，家勝業裏，為天下高貲。

translations.literal: His family for generations was registered in the Shence Army; they lived on Shengye Lane and were among the wealthiest in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been enrolled in the Shence Army; they lived on Shengye Lane and ranked among the richest households in the empire.

sentences.zh: 父宗，巧射利，侈靡自奉，僮千人，以此奮，累除檢校司空、金吾大將軍，遙領興元節度使。

translations.literal: His father Zong was skilled at archery and profit, lived in extravagant self-indulgence with a thousand servants, and through this rose repeatedly to Acting Grand Mentor, Golden Crow grand general, and titular military governor of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zong was a crack archer and shrewd profiteer who maintained a household of a thousand servants in lavish style; on that foundation he rose to Acting Grand Mentor, Golden Crow grand general, and titular governor of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 處存自右軍鎮使歷檢校刑部尚書、定州制置使，累遷義武節度使。

translations.literal: Chucun rose from Right Army garrison commander through Acting Minister of Justice and Dingzhou establishment commissioner to repeated promotion as military governor of Yiwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun advanced from Right Army garrison commander through Acting Minister of Justice and commissioner for the Dingzhou establishment to military governor of the Yiwu Army.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷京師，處存號哭，不俟詔，分麾下兵二千間道至山南衛乘輿。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao seized the capital, Chucun wailed in grief; without awaiting an edict he divided two thousand troops under his command by hidden routes to the south of the mountains to guard the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took the capital, Chucun wept aloud; without waiting for orders he sent two thousand of his men by hidden routes into the southern mountains to protect the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 外約王重榮連盟，進屯渭橋，而涇州行軍司馬唐弘夫亦屯渭北。

translations.literal: Externally he arranged alliance with Wang Chongrong, advanced to garrison Weiqiao, while the Jingzhou campaign deputy Tang Hongfu also encamped north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He secured an alliance with Wang Chongrong, advanced to Weiqiao, while Jingzhou campaign deputy Tang Hongfu encamped on the north bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔處存檢校尚書右仆射督戰，俄拜東南面行營招討使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chucun Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat to supervise the campaign; soon he was named southeastern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat to direct operations, and soon afterward southeastern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 中和二年授京城東面都統。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe he was appointed eastern metropolitan commander of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe he was made eastern metropolitan commander for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 每痛國難未夷，語輒流涕，軍中多處存義，愈為之用。

translations.literal: Whenever he grieved that the national calamity was not yet settled, his words ended in tears; the army largely followed Chucun's sense of righteousness and was all the more devoted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of the unredeemed national crisis he wept; his troops took their cue from his moral fervor and fought all the harder for him.

sentences.zh: 素善李克用，又故婚好，遣使十輩曉譬迎勸，卒共平京師。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Li Keyong and was also connected by an old marriage alliance; he sent ten envoys in succession to explain, welcome, and persuade him, and in the end they jointly pacified the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Li Keyong and was linked by marriage as well; he sent ten successive embassies to reason with him and win his cooperation, and together they recovered the capital.

sentences.zh: 王鐸差興復功，以勤王舉義處存為第一，收城破賊克用為第一。

translations.literal: Wang Duo ranked restoration achievements: for raising troops in loyal service Chucun was first, for recovering the city and defeating bandits Keyong was first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo ranked the contributors to the restoration: Chucun first for rallying loyal forces, Li Keyong first for retaking the city and crushing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校司空。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 復出兵三千屬大將張公慶會諸軍捕巢泰山，滅之。

translations.literal: He again sent out three thousand troops under the great general Zhang Gongqing to join the various armies in hunting Huang Chao on Mount Tai and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched another three thousand men under his chief general Zhang Gongqing to join the allied forces in hunting Huang Chao on Mount Tai until he was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Minister of Works and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Acting Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 田令孜討王重榮，徙處存節度河中，上書言：「重榮有大功，不可改易，搖諸侯之心。」

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi campaigned against Wang Chongrong and transferred Chucun to govern Hedong; Chucun memorialized saying, "Chongrong has great merit and must not be changed—this would shake the hearts of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Lingzi moved against Wang Chongrong, Chucun was reassigned to Hedong; he memorialized, "Chongrong has rendered great service; to displace him now would unsettle every regional commander.

sentences.zh: 不納，趣上道。

translations.literal: It was not accepted; he was urged to take the road.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored his plea and ordered him to depart at once.

sentences.zh: 軍次晉州，刺史冀君武閉門不內，而重榮拒詔。

translations.literal: When the army reached Jin Prefecture, the prefect Ji Junwu shut the gates and would not admit them, while Chongrong defied the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When his army reached Jinzhou, Prefect Ji Junwu barred the gates, and Chongrong openly defied the transfer order.

sentences.zh: 處存臨事通便宜，有大將風。

translations.literal: Chucun in affairs grasped what was expedient and had the bearing of a great commander.
translations.idiomatic: In affairs of state Chucun knew when to bend the rules and carried himself like a great commander.

sentences.zh: 幽、鎮兵悍馬強，其地勢也，而易定介於其間，侵軼歲至。

translations.literal: You and Zhen had fierce troops and strong horses by the nature of their terrain, while Yiding lay between them and suffered yearly raids.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou and Zhenzhou boasted fierce troops and powerful horses by the logic of geography, while Yiding lay sandwiched between them and endured yearly incursions.

sentences.zh: 及李匡威得誌，謀並取之。

translations.literal: When Li Kuangwei achieved his ambition, he plotted to seize it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Kuangwei had his way, he plotted to swallow the territory whole.

sentences.zh: 處存善修鄰歡，內撫民有恩，痛折節下賢，協穆太原以自助，遠近同心。

translations.literal: Chucun was skilled at cultivating neighborly goodwill, inwardly comforted the people with kindness, earnestly humbled himself to recruit the worthy, harmonized with Taiyuan to aid himself, and near and far were of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun cultivated good relations with his neighbors, ruled his people with kindness, humbled himself to recruit talent, and aligned with Taiyuan for mutual support until allies near and far stood with him as one.

sentences.zh: 歲時講兵，與諸鎮抗，無能侵軋者。

translations.literal: Each year he drilled troops and resisted the various commands; none could press or raid him.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his forces every year and held his own against the neighboring commands until none could harry his borders.

sentences.zh: 累加侍中、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly given Palace Attendant and Acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly honored as Palace Attendant and Acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈太子太師，謚曰忠肅。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-five; he was posthumously given Heir Apparent Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 三軍跡河朔舊事，推子郜由副使為留後，昭宗從之。

translations.literal: The three armies followed the old Hebei practice and pushed his son Gao from deputy commissioner to acting governor; Emperor Zhaozong consented.
translations.idiomatic: Following the old Hebei custom, the army installed his son Gao from deputy commissioner to acting governor, and Emperor Zhaozong approved.

sentences.zh: 累拜節度使，加檢校司空、同中書門下平章事，又進太保。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed military governor, given Acting Grand Mentor and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and further advanced to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was confirmed as military governor, made Acting Grand Mentor and Grand Councilor, and later advanced to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，朱全忠使張存敬攻幽州，以瓦橋濘潦，道祁溝關。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua, Zhu Quanzhong sent Zhang Cunjing to attack Youzhou; because the Waqiao marshes were flooded and mired, they took the route through Qigou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guanghua (900), Zhu Quanzhong dispatched Zhang Cunjing against Youzhou. The marshes around Waqiao were deep with floodwater, so the army turned aside and marched by way of Qigou Pass.

sentences.zh: 郜方與劉守光厚，乃畀叔處直兵擾其尾，令騎將甄瓊章次義豐，而存敬遊弈騎已至，且戰且引十餘里，執瓊章。

translations.literal: Gao was then on close terms with Liu Shouguang; he gave his uncle Chuzhi troops to harass their rear, ordered the cavalry general Zhen Qionzhang to encamp at Yifeng, but Cunjing's ranging cavalry had already arrived—fighting as they withdrew for more than ten li, they captured Qionzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was on friendly terms with Liu Shouguang. He gave his uncle Wang Chuzhi a force to harry the enemy's rear and posted the cavalry commander Zhen Qionzhang at Yifeng. But Zhang Cunjing's scouting horsemen were already there; they fought as they fell back for more than ten li and took Qionzhang captive.

sentences.zh: 而氏叔琮下深澤，執大將馬少安，圍祁州，屠之，斬刺史楊約，休兵十日。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shi Shuzong descended upon Shenze, captured the great general Ma Shao'an, besieged Qizhou, slaughtered it, beheaded the prefect Yang Yue, and rested the army ten days.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Shi Shuzong pushed into Shenze, seized the great general Ma Shao'an, and besieged Qizhou. The city was put to the sword, Prefect Yang Yue was executed, and the army halted for ten days.

sentences.zh: 處直壁沙河，存敬軍河北，挑戰，處直不出，涉河乃戰，處直大敗，亡大將十五，士死者數萬。

translations.literal: Chuzhi fortified at Shahe; Cunjing's army was north of the river and offered battle; Chuzhi did not come out; Cunjing crossed the river and then fought; Chuzhi was greatly defeated, losing fifteen great generals, and soldiers dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuzhi held a fortified camp at Shahe while Zhang Cunjing's army stood north of the river and challenged him. Chuzhi refused to engage until Cunjing forded the river; then Chuzhi was routed, losing fifteen chief commanders and tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 存敬收械甲以賦戰士，而焚其餘，遂圍定州。

translations.literal: Cunjing collected weapons and armor to distribute to the warriors, burned the remainder, and then besieged Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunjing gathered captured arms and armor to equip his soldiers, burned what remained, and laid siege to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 郜斬親吏梁汶，移書存敬，且請盟。

translations.literal: Gao executed his close attendant Liang Wen, sent a letter to Cunjing, and moreover requested an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao executed his personal officer Liang Wen, wrote to Zhang Cunjing, and asked for peace.

sentences.zh: 俄而外郛陷，郜以其族奔太原，使處直主留後。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the outer wall fell; Gao fled with his clan to Taiyuan and had Chuzhi take charge as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the outer city fell. Gao fled with his clan to Taiyuan and left Wang Chuzhi behind as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 全忠亦至，處直辭曰：「弊邑事上未嘗不忠，事鄰未嘗不禮，弗虞君之見攻也。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong also arrived; Chuzhi apologized, saying: "Our humble territory has never been disloyal in serving the sovereign, nor discourteous in dealings with neighbors; we did not anticipate Your Lordship's attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong arrived in person. Wang Chuzhi pleaded: "Our domain has always served the throne faithfully and treated our neighbors with courtesy. We never imagined you would turn your armies against us.

sentences.zh: 全忠責何故事克用，答曰：「太原藉兄弟之舊，修好往來，常道也。

translations.literal: Quanzhong reproached him: "Why do you serve Li Keyong?" He replied: "Taiyuan and we rely on old ties as brothers; maintaining friendly relations and mutual visits is the ordinary way.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong demanded why he maintained relations with Li Keyong. Chuzhi answered, "Taiyuan and we are bound by long-standing ties as close as brothers; friendly exchanges are only natural.

sentences.zh: 君茍為罪，請改圖。」

translations.literal: If Your Lordship deem this a crime, I beg to change course."
translations.idiomatic: If you judge that a fault, I am ready to mend my ways."

sentences.zh: 全忠許之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong accepted.

sentences.zh: 處直以從孫為質，上所持節，即獻絹三十萬，具牛酒犒師。

translations.literal: Chuzhi offered his nephew's son as hostage, surrendered the credentials of office he held, and immediately presented three hundred thousand bolts of silk, providing oxen and wine to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuzhi sent a grandnephew as hostage, handed over his commission, and at once submitted three hundred thousand bolts of silk with cattle and wine to feast the army.

sentences.zh: 存敬取成而還。

translations.literal: Cunjing achieved his aims and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunjing, having secured what he came for, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 全忠表處直為節度留後、檢校尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized the throne to appoint Chuzhi acting military commissioner and honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong recommended Wang Chuzhi as acting military governor and honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 郜至太原，克用表為檢校太尉，卒。

translations.literal: Gao reached Taiyuan; Li Keyong memorialized him as honorary Grand Preceptor; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao reached Taiyuan, where Li Keyong had him appointed honorary Grand Preceptor. He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 處直，字允明，天復初為太原郡王。

translations.literal: Chuzhi, courtesy name Yunming, at the beginning of the Tianfu era became Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuzhi, styled Yunming, was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan at the opening of the Tianfu reign.

sentences.zh: 鄧處訥，字沖韞，邵州龍潭人。

translations.literal: Deng Chuna, courtesy name Chongyun, was a native of Longtan in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chuna, styled Chongyun, came from Longtan in Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 少從江西人閔頊防秋安南。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the Jiangxi man Min Xu in the autumn garrison defense of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he followed Min Xu of Jiangxi to Annam on the autumn defense rotation.

sentences.zh: 中和元年還，道潭州，逐觀察使李裕，召諸州戍校徇曰：「天下未定，今與君等安護州邑，以待天子命，若何？」

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhonghe he returned, passed through Tanzhou, expelled the observation commissioner Li Yu, gathered the garrison officers of the various prefectures and declared: "The realm is not yet settled; now let us together secure and protect our prefectures and districts, awaiting the Son of Heaven's command—what say you?
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhonghe (881) he came home by way of Tanzhou, drove out Observation Commissioner Li Yu, and summoned the garrison commanders. "The empire is still unsettled," he said. "Let us defend our districts until the Son of Heaven gives his orders. What do you say?

sentences.zh: 眾稱善。

translations.literal: The crowd said it was good.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃推頊為留後，請諸朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon they supported Xu as acting commissioner and requested confirmation from the court.
translations.idiomatic: They raised Min Xu as acting governor and petitioned the court for confirmation.

sentences.zh: 僖宗方在蜀，遣使者撫慰。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong was then in Shu and sent envoys to console and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong was in Shu and dispatched envoys to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 當是時，撫州刺史鐘傳據洪州，議者欲二盜相噬，即復置鎮南軍，擢頊節度使。

translations.literal: At that time Zhong Chuan, prefect of Fuzhou, held Hongzhou; the advisers wished the two bandits would devour each other, and so restored the Zhennan Army and promoted Xu to military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chuan of Fuzhou held Hongzhou. Court strategists hoped the two renegades would destroy each other, revived the Zhennan Army, and elevated Min Xu to military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 頊悟，不受命。

translations.literal: Xu understood and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Min Xu saw through the design and refused the commission.

sentences.zh: 更為檢校尚書右仆射、欽化軍節度使，以處訥為邵州刺史。

translations.literal: He was instead made honorary Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Qinhua Army military commissioner, with Chuna appointed prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was instead made honorary Right Vice Director and governor of the Qinhua Army, while Deng Chuna became prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 朗州武陵人雷滿者，本漁師，有勇力。

translations.literal: Lei Man of Wuling in Langzhou was originally a fisherman and possessed courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man of Wuling in Langzhou had begun as a fisherman but was bold and powerful.

sentences.zh: 時武陵諸蠻數叛，荊南節度使高駢擢滿為裨將，將鎮蠻軍從駢淮南。

translations.literal: At the time the various Man of Wuling frequently rebelled; the Jingnan military commissioner Gao Pian promoted Man to assistant general and had him lead the garrison Man army following Pian to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples around Wuling were in constant revolt. Jingnan Governor Gao Pian promoted Lei Man and took him south to Huainan at the head of the frontier Man troops.

sentences.zh: 逃歸，與裏人區景思獵大澤中，嘯亡命少年千人，署伍長，自號「朗團軍」。

translations.literal: He fled back, and with his fellow townsman Qu Jingsi hunted in the great marshes, rallied a thousand young outlaws, appointed squad leaders, and styled themselves the "Lang Tuan Army."
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man deserted home. In the great marshes he and Qu Jingsi gathered a thousand desperate youths, organized squad chiefs, and called themselves the Lang Regiment.

sentences.zh: 推滿為帥，景思為司馬，襲州，殺刺史崔翥。

translations.literal: They made Man commander and Jingsi marshal, raided the prefecture, and killed Prefect Cui Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed Lei Man chief and Qu Jingsi marshal, seized the prefectural seat, and killed Prefect Cui Zhu.

sentences.zh: 詔授朗州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting Langzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court recognized him as acting military governor of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲略江陵，焚廬落，劫居人。

translations.literal: Each year he raided Jiangling, burning villages and plundering residents.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he raided Jiangling, burning homesteads and carrying off the people.

sentences.zh: 俄進武貞軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was advanced to Wuzhen Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to military governor of the Wuzhen Army.

sentences.zh: 先是，陬溪人周嶽與滿狎，因獵宰肉不平而鬥，欲殺滿，不克。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Yue of Zouxi was intimate with Man; while hunting they quarreled over unequal division of butchered meat and fought; Yue tried to kill Man but failed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yue of Zouxi had been intimate with Lei Man until a hunt ended in a quarrel over unequal shares of butchered game; Yue tried to kill him and failed.

sentences.zh: 見滿已據州，悉眾趨衡州，逐刺史徐顥，詔授衡州刺史。

translations.literal: Seeing Man had seized the prefecture, he led all his followers to Hengzhou, expelled Prefect Xu Hao, and was edict-appointed prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Lei Man took Langzhou, Zhou Yue marched to Hengzhou, drove out Prefect Xu Hao, and received an edict as prefect.

sentences.zh: 石門峒酋向瑰聞滿得誌，亦集夷獠數千，屠牛勞眾，操長刀柘弩寇州縣，自稱「朗北團」。

translations.literal: The cave chief Xiang Gui of Shimen, hearing Man had achieved his ambition, also gathered several thousand Yi and Liao tribesmen, slaughtered oxen to feast the multitude, wielding long blades and catalpa-wood crossbows to raid prefectures and counties, styling himself "Langbei Tuan."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Gui of Shimen heard of Lei Man's success and mustered thousands of tribal warriors, feasted them with slaughtered oxen, armed them with long swords and catalpa crossbows, and raided the region as the Northern Lang Regiment.

sentences.zh: 陷澧州，殺刺史呂自牧，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: He captured Lizhou, killed Prefect Lu Zimu, and styled himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He took Lizhou, killed Prefect Lu Zimu, and declared himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 頊既強大，且治人有恩，哀徐顥窮，率兵納之。

translations.literal: Xu had grown powerful and moreover governed with kindness toward the people; pitying Xu Hao's desperate plight, he led troops to restore him.
translations.idiomatic: Min Xu had grown strong and ruled with kindness. Moved by Xu Hao's exile, he led an army to restore him.

sentences.zh: 向瑰召梅山十峒獠斷邵州道，頊掩其營。

translations.literal: Xiang Gui summoned the Liao of the ten Meishan cave chiefs to block the Shaozhou road; Xu ambushed his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Gui called up Meishan tribesmen to cut the road to Shaozhou; Min Xu fell on his camp by surprise.

sentences.zh: 周嶽羸軍誘戰，頊墮伏中，故大敗。

translations.literal: Zhou Yue deployed a weakened force to lure battle; Xu fell into an ambush and therefore suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yue sent a weakened force to draw him on; Min Xu walked into an ambush and was routed.

sentences.zh: 淮西將黃皓殺頊。

translations.literal: The Huaixi general Huang Hao killed Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao, a Huaixi officer, killed Min Xu.

sentences.zh: 嶽聞亂，以輕兵入潭州，自稱欽化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Yue heard of the turmoil and entered Tanzhou with light troops, declaring himself Qinhua Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yue swept into Tanzhou with a light force and proclaimed himself governor of the Qinhua Army.

sentences.zh: 盧訥聞之哭，諸將入吊。

translations.literal: Lu Ne heard and wept; the generals entered to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ne wept when he heard; his generals came to mourn with him.

sentences.zh: 處訥曰：「與君等荷仆射恩，若合一州之兵問周嶽罪，奈何？」

translations.literal: Chuna said: "You and I have received the Vice Minister's grace; if we gather the armies of the whole prefecture to demand Zhou Yue answer for his crime, what say you?
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chuna said, "We owe our positions to the Vice Minister's favor. If we rally every soldier in the prefecture and call Zhou Yue to account—are you with me?"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The men said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: We are," they answered.

sentences.zh: 於是礪甲訓兵，積八年，結雷滿為援，攻嶽斬之，自稱留後。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sharpened armor and drilled troops; over eight years they allied with Lei Man as support, attacked Yue and beheaded him, and Chuna declared himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They sharpened armor and drilled for eight years, secured Lei Man as ally, beheaded Zhou Yue, and Deng Chuna declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 昭宗詔拜武安軍節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong edict-appointed him Wuan Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong confirmed him as military governor of the Wuan Army.

sentences.zh: 不三日，會劉建鋒、馬殷兵至，攻澧陵，處訥遣邵州豪傑蔣勛、鄧繼崇率兵三千斷龍回關。

translations.literal: Within three days, Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin's troops arrived and attacked Liling; Chuna sent the Shaozhou men-of-distinction Jiang Xun and Deng Jichong to lead three thousand men to block Longhui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Less than three days later Liu Jianfeng and Ma Yin attacked Liling. Deng Chuna sent Jiang Xun and Deng Jichong with three thousand men to hold Longhui Pass.

sentences.zh: 勛以牛酒犒師，殷說勛曰：「劉公勇智絕人，術家言當興翼、軫間。

translations.literal: Xun used oxen and wine to feast the troops; Yin persuaded Xun, saying: "Lord Liu's courage and wisdom surpass all men; geomancers say he is destined to rise between the Wings and Chariot constellations.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xun feasted his men with cattle and wine. Ma Yin took him aside: "Liu Jianfeng's courage and cunning are unmatched; diviners say his fortune lies among the Wings and Chariot stars over Hunan.

sentences.zh: 今精兵十萬，攻必下，戰必克，收敗眾以餉軍，公裒鄉兵捍關，殆矣。

translations.literal: Now with a hundred thousand elite troops, every siege he takes, every battle he wins; he would gather the defeated masses to supply his army—you, assembling local militia to hold a pass, are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: He commands a hundred thousand seasoned troops; every city falls, every battle he wins. He will press the defeated into his ranks. You, with country militia at a pass—you are finished.

sentences.zh: 不如下之，富貴可得也。」

translations.literal: Better to submit; wealth and honor may be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yield now, while rank and riches can still be yours.

sentences.zh: 勛謂然。

translations.literal: Xun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xun was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 又其下畏建鋒虐，夜棄甲走。

translations.literal: Moreover his subordinates feared Jianfeng's cruelty; at night they cast off armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His men also feared Liu Jianfeng's brutality and deserted by night.

sentences.zh: 建鋒至關，曰：「此天意也！」

translations.literal: Jianfeng reached the pass and said: "This is Heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jianfeng reached the pass he cried, "Heaven itself has opened the way!

sentences.zh: 盡用邵旗鎧趨潭州。

translations.literal: He used Shaozhou banners and armor in full and rushed toward Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Tanzhou flying Shaozhou colors and wearing captured armor.

sentences.zh: 守者以為勛軍，納之。

translations.literal: The defenders thought it was Xun's army and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison took them for Jiang Xun's troops and let them in.

sentences.zh: 既入，處訥方宴，執而殺之。

translations.literal: Once inside, Chuna was at a banquet; they seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chuna was still at banquet when they seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 建鋒許勛賞，未及行，遣請，弗許，勛怒，率鄧繼崇攻湘鄉，取邵州，進壁定勝、武安。

translations.literal: Jianfeng promised Xun rewards, but before they could be carried out he sent to request them and was refused; Xun grew angry and with Deng Jichong attacked Xiangxiang, took Shaozhou, and advanced to encamp at Dingsheng and Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianfeng promised Jiang Xun rewards but reneged; enraged, Xun joined Deng Jichong, seized Xiangxiang and Shaozhou, and encamped at Dingsheng and Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 建鋒使殷督諸將擊之，殷大敗，走江滸。

translations.literal: Jianfeng sent Yin to supervise the generals in attacking them; Yin was greatly defeated and fled to the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianfeng sent Ma Yin against them; Yin was routed and fled to the riverside.

sentences.zh: 鄉人夏侯陟教殷以奇兵出迪田，逾澗山，據江為壁，伏兵於莽，誘勛度江。

translations.literal: His townsman Xiahou Shi taught Yin to send an odd force out by Ditian, cross the mountain streams, hold the river as a wall, set ambush in the thickets, and lure Xun to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman, Xiahou Shi, advised Ma Yin to send a flanking force through Ditian, cross the mountain streams, fortify the riverbank, hide troops in the brush, and lure Jiang Xun across the water.

sentences.zh: 勛見士未陣，爭出鬥，殷分兵襲其壁，麾瀕江軍夾擊，勛大敗，拔定勝一壁，進圍邵州。

translations.literal: Xun saw the troops not yet in formation and rushed out to fight; Yin divided his force to strike their camp, commanded the riverbank troops to attack from both sides, and Xun was greatly defeated; he took the Dingsheng camp and advanced to besiege Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xun saw the enemy not yet formed and charged out; Yin split his force to strike the camp and ordered the river troops to attack from both flanks. Xun was crushed; Yin took Dingsheng and besieged Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 未下而建鋒死，殷代為節度使。

translations.literal: Before it fell Jianfeng died, and Yin succeeded as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shaozhou fell, Liu Jianfeng died and Ma Yin became military governor.

sentences.zh: 勛請和，不許，卒禽勛斬之。

translations.literal: Xun requested peace and was refused; in the end he was captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xun sued for peace but was refused; he was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 是時，道州蠻酋蔡結、何庾，衡人楊師遠各據州叛。

translations.literal: At that time the Man chiefs of Daozhou, Cai Jie and He Yu, and the Heng man Yang Shiyuan each held their prefectures in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Daozhou chieftains Cai Jie and He Yu and the Hengzhou rebel Yang Shiyuan each held their prefectures in revolt.

sentences.zh: 宿人魯景仁從黃巢為盜，至廣州，病不能去，以千騎留連州，眾饑，從蔡結求糧，乃相倚杖，與州戍將黃行存誘工商四五千人據連州。

translations.literal: The Su man Lu Jingren had followed Huang Chao as a bandit to Guangzhou; unable to leave because of illness, he remained with a thousand horsemen at Lianzhou; the masses were starving; he sought grain from Cai Jie and thus relied on each other, and with the garrison general Huang Xingcun induced four or five thousand merchants and artisans to seize Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingren of Suzhou had ridden with Huang Chao; stranded sick at Guangzhou, he kept a thousand horsemen at Lianzhou. When famine struck, he allied with Cai Jie and, with garrison officer Huang Xingcun, rallied merchants to seize the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 郴人陳彥謙殺刺史董嶽，發官帑募士，自稱都統，勝兵四千。

translations.literal: Chen Yanqian of Chenzhou killed Prefect Dong Yue, opened the official treasury to recruit troops, styled himself supreme commander, and had four thousand victorious troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yanqian of Chenzhou killed Prefect Dong Yue, spent the treasury to raise troops, styled himself supreme commander, and fielded four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 零陵人唐行旻乘巢亂，脅眾自防，盜永州，殺刺史鄭蔚，與景仁合從，數遣諜殷虛實，完壘自守。

translations.literal: Tang Xingmin of Lingling took advantage of Chao's chaos to coerce the masses for self-defense, plundered Yongzhou, killed Prefect Zheng Wei, joined with Jingren, and repeatedly sent spies to probe Yin's strength, fortifying camps to hold their ground.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xingmin of Lingling exploited the chaos to arm a mob, seized Yongzhou and killed Prefect Zheng Wei, allied with Lu Jingren, spied on Ma Yin's strength, and held fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 殷遣將李瓊攻永州，殺行旻。

translations.literal: Yin sent the general Li Qiong to attack Yongzhou and killed Xingmin.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin sent Li Qiong against Yongzhou and killed Tang Xingmin.

sentences.zh: 李瑭攻道州，蔡結約峒獠為援，久不勝，謀曰：「蠻所恃，林藪耳。」

translations.literal: Li Tang attacked Daozhou; Cai Jie allied with cave Liao as support; for long he could not win; he said: "What the Man rely on is forest and marsh alone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang besieged Daozhou; Cai Jie called cave tribes to his aid. After long stalemate Tang said, "The tribesmen depend on nothing but woods and thickets.

sentences.zh: 乃屯大川，伐山焚林，獠驚走。

translations.literal: He then encamped on the great river, felled mountains and burned forests, and the Liao fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: He camped on the open river plain, cut and burned the forests, and the tribesmen fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 城陷，執蔡結、何庾，殷斬之。

translations.literal: The city fell; Cai Jie and He Yu were captured; Yin beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell; Cai Jie and He Yu were taken and Ma Yin executed them.

sentences.zh: 李瓊出耒陽、常寧，攻郴州，陳彥謙出戰，軍亂不能陣，斬彥謙。

translations.literal: Li Qiong went out through Leiyang and Changning to attack Chenzhou; Chen Yanqian came out to fight; the army fell into disorder and could not form ranks; Yanqian was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong marched through Leiyang and Changning against Chenzhou; Chen Yanqian met him in battle but his ranks broke; he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 進圍連州，魯景仁乘城守，三日不下，夜焚其門入之，景仁自刺死。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Lianzhou; Lu Jingren defended from the walls; for three days it did not fall; at night they burned the gate and entered; Jingren stabbed himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Lianzhou lasted three days; Lu Jingren held the walls until attackers burned the gate at night; Jingren took his own life.

sentences.zh: 頊，字公謹。

translations.literal: Xu, courtesy name Gongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Min Xu, styled Gongjin.

sentences.zh: 滿，字秉仁。

translations.literal: Man, courtesy name Bingren.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man, styled Bingren.

sentences.zh: 嶽，字峻昭。

translations.literal: Yue, courtesy name Junzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yue, styled Junzhao.

sentences.zh: 行旻，字昌圖。

translations.literal: Xingmin, courtesy name Changtu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xingmin, styled Changtu.

sentences.zh: 滿不修飭，每宴使客，抵寶器潭中，曰：「此水府也，蛟龍所憑，吾能沒焉。」

translations.literal: Man was careless in deportment; whenever he feasted and entertained guests he would cast precious vessels into the pool, saying: "This is the water palace; dragons dwell here; I can dive among them.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man cared nothing for propriety. At feasts he would hurl precious vessels into a pool and declare, "This is the dragon palace—I can dive to its bottom.

sentences.zh: 乃裸入水，俄取器以出。

translations.literal: He then stripped and entered the water, and shortly brought the vessels out.
translations.idiomatic: He would strip, plunge in, and moments later surface with the treasures.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to honorary Grand Preceptor and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to honorary Grand Preceptor and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 天復元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 子彥威自立。

translations.literal: His son Yanwei established himself [in power].
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanwei seized power on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 間荊南節度使成汭兵出。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Jingnan military commissioner Cheng Ru's troops marched out.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile troops of Jingnan Governor Cheng Ru marched out.

sentences.zh: 襲江陵，入之，焚樓船，殘墟落，數千里無人跡。

translations.literal: They raided Jiangling, entered it, burned tower ships, ravaged villages, and for several thousand li there was no trace of human habitation.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Jiangling, burned the tower ships, laid waste to the countryside, and left thousands of li without a living soul.

sentences.zh: 弟彥恭，結忠義節度趙匡凝以逐彥威，據江陵。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yangong joined with Zhongyi Army governor Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei and seize Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yan Gong allied with Zhao Kuangning of the Zhongyi Army to expel Yanwei and hold Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 匡凝弟匡明擊之，還走朗州。

translations.literal: Kuangning's younger brother Kuangming attacked them; they fled back to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming attacked them and they fled back to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬玫署儒領府事。

translations.literal: Jingmei appointed Ru to head prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmei appointed Ru to administer the prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷檢校工部尚書，為節度使，進檢校右仆射。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works and made military commissioner, then advanced to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Acting Minister of Works and military governor, then Acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 敬玫有悍卒三千，號「忠勇軍」，暴甚，儒不能制。

translations.literal: Jingmei had three thousand fierce troops styled the "Loyal and Brave Army," extremely violent; Ru could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmei had three thousand brutal troops called the Loyal and Brave Army; Ru could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 初，紹業將申屠琮率兵五千援京師，既歸，儒告以忠勇撓治，琮請除之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shaoye was about to send Shen Tuqiong with five thousand troops to aid the capital; after his return Ru reported that the Loyal and Brave were disrupting governance, and Tuqiong requested their removal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shaoye had sent Shen Tuqiong with five thousand men to aid the capital. On his return Ru complained the Loyal and Brave were ruining order; Tuqiong asked to eliminate them.

sentences.zh: 大將程君從聞之，率眾奔澧州，琮追斬百餘人，軍乃潰。

translations.literal: The great general Cheng Juncong heard of it and led the masses to flee to Lizhou; Tuqiong pursued and beheaded more than a hundred men, and the army then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: General Cheng Juncong heard and fled to Lizhou with his men; Tuqiong pursued and killed over a hundred before the corps broke up.

sentences.zh: 已而琮復顓軍。

translations.literal: Before long Tuqiong again dominated the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shen Tuqiong again dominated the army.

sentences.zh: 雷滿三以兵薄城，儒厚啖以利，乃去。

translations.literal: Lei Man three times pressed the city with troops; Ru richly rewarded him with profit and he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man thrice besieged the city; Ru bought him off with lavish gifts and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 淮南將張瑰、韓師德據復、嶽二州，自署刺史。

translations.literal: The Huainan generals Zhang Gui and Han Shide held Fu and Yue prefectures and appointed themselves prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan generals Zhang Gui and Han Shide held Fu and Yue and styled themselves prefects.

sentences.zh: 儒請瑰攝行軍司馬，師德攝節度副使，共擊滿。

translations.literal: Ru requested Gui act as campaign deputy and Shide as deputy military commissioner, and together they attacked Man.
translations.idiomatic: Ru asked Gui to serve as campaign deputy and Shide as deputy governor; together they attacked Lei Man.

sentences.zh: 師德兵上峽，大略去。

translations.literal: Shide's troops went up the gorges and largely departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shide's men entered the gorges but mostly drifted away.

sentences.zh: 瑰引兵逐儒，儒將奔行在，既又劫還，囚之。

translations.literal: Gui led troops to pursue Ru; Ru was about to flee to the imperial court, but was seized and brought back and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui turned on Ru, who tried to flee to court but was seized and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 瑰，滑州人，暴勇而殘，荊故將夷戮幾盡。

translations.literal: Gui was a man of Huazhou, violent and brave but cruel; he nearly exterminated the old Jing generals.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was from Huazhou, fierce and cruel; he almost wiped out the former Jingnan commanders.

sentences.zh: 時以楊玄晦代敬玫監軍，召敬玫還成都，懼帝治前罪，稱疾自解。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Xuanhui was sent to replace Jingmei as army monitor; Jingmei was recalled to Chengdu; fearing punishment for earlier crimes, he pleaded illness to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanhui replaced Jingmei as army monitor; Jingmei was recalled to Chengdu but, fearing prosecution, pleaded illness to resign.

sentences.zh: 前此數殺大將富商，故積賄，每曝衣，紈繡不可計。

translations.literal: Before this he had several times killed great generals and wealthy merchants, and so amassed bribes; whenever he aired his clothes, silks and brocades were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He had killed many generals and rich merchants and amassed bribes; when he aired his wardrobe, brocades beyond counting were spread out.

sentences.zh: 瑰見心動，遣卒賊之。

translations.literal: Gui saw it and his heart was moved; he sent soldiers to rob him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui saw the display and sent men to rob him.

sentences.zh: 敬玫衣黃衣，盜刺其腹死。

translations.literal: Jingmei wore yellow clothes; a thief secretly stabbed his belly and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmei wore yellow robes; an assassin stabbed him in the abdomen and killed him.

sentences.zh: 秦宗言來寇，馬步使趙匡欲奉儒出，瑰覺之，殺匡而絕儒食，七日死。

translations.literal: Qin Zongyan came to attack; the horse-and-foot commissioner Zhao Kuang wished to escort Ru out; Gui discovered it, killed Kuang, and cut off Ru's food supply—Ru died after seven days.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongyan raided the city, the cavalry-and-infantry commissioner Zhao Kuang tried to smuggle Ru out. Zhang Gui found out, killed Kuang, and starved Ru to death within seven days.

sentences.zh: 瑰固壘二歲，樵蘇皆盡，米鬥錢四十千，計抔而食，號為「通腸」。

translations.literal: Gui held the fortress for two years; firewood and kindling were all exhausted; rice was forty thousand cash per dou; they measured out handfuls to eat, calling it "Clearing the Intestines."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui held the fort for two years until firewood and fuel were gone. Rice reached forty thousand cash per dou; the garrison rationed food by the cupful in a portion they nicknamed "Gut Passage."

sentences.zh: 疫死者，爭啖其屍，縣首於戶以備饌。

translations.literal: Those who died of plague—people fought to eat their corpses; heads were hung at doorways as provisions.
translations.idiomatic: People fought over the bodies of those who died in the epidemic, and heads were hung at doorways to serve as food.

sentences.zh: 軍中甲鼓無遺，夜擊闔為警。

translations.literal: In the army no armor or drums remained; at night they beat the city gates as an alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The army had no armor or drums left; at night they struck the city gates to sound the alarm.

sentences.zh: 宗言不能下，乃解去。

translations.literal: Zongyan could not take the city, so he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan failed to capture the city and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二年，宗權遣趙德諲攻瑰，瑰求救於歸州刺史郭禹，禹率峽州刺史潘章解圍。

translations.literal: In the second year, Zongquan sent Zhao Deyin to attack Gui; Gui sought rescue from Guizhou prefect Guo Yu; Yu led Xiazhou prefect Pan Zhang to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Qin Zongquan sent Zhao Deyin against Zhang Gui. Gui appealed to Guo Yu, prefect of Guizhou, who marched with Xiazhou prefect Pan Zhang to break the siege.

sentences.zh: 明年，德諲又至，諸將困於戰，城遂陷，瑰死，人無識者，並屍於井。

translations.literal: The next year Deyin came again; the generals were worn down in battle; the city then fell; Gui died, with no one to recognize him; bodies were piled together in a well.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Deyin returned. The defenders were exhausted by fighting, the city fell, and Gui was killed—so unrecognizable that his corpse was thrown into a well with the others.

sentences.zh: 復州長史陳璠從瑰至江陵，密斷瑰首置囊中，走京師獻之，授安州刺史。

translations.literal: Fuzhou chief secretary Chen Fan followed Gui to Jiangling, secretly cut off Gui's head and put it in a bag, fled to the capital and presented it, and was appointed prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan, chief secretary of Fuzhou, accompanied Gui to Jiangling, secretly severed his head and carried it in a bag to the capital as a trophy. He was rewarded with appointment as prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉巨容，徐州人。

translations.literal: Liu Jurong was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jurong was a native of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為州大將。

translations.literal: He served as a prefectural great general.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a senior military officer of his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 龐勛之反，自拔歸，授埇橋鎮遏使。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled, he broke away and returned home on his own, and was appointed Yongqiao garrison commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rebelled, he deserted and made his way home, and was appointed commissioner for suppressing unrest at Yongqiao.

sentences.zh: 浙西突陣將王郢反，攻明州，巨容以筒箭射郢死，拜明州刺史，徙楚州團練使。

translations.literal: Wang Ying, the Zhexi shock-column general, rebelled and attacked Mingzhou; Jurong shot Ying dead with a tube-arrow; he was appointed Mingzhou prefect and transferred to be Chuzhou regimental commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ying, the Zhexi shock-troop commander, rebelled and attacked Mingzhou, Jurong killed him with a bolt from a tube-bow. He was made prefect of Mingzhou and later transferred to regimental commissioner of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 黃巢亂江淮，授蘄黃招討副使，徙襄州行軍司馬、檢校右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In Huang Chao's turmoil in the Jiang-Huai region, he was appointed deputy pacification commissioner for Qi and Huang, then transferred to be Xiangzhou marching commissioner and acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's uprising in the Jiang-Huai region, he was made deputy pacification commissioner for Qi and Huang, then promoted to marching commissioner of Xiangzhou and acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 巢據荊南，俄遷山南東道節度使以捍巢，屯團林。

translations.literal: Chao occupied Jingnan; shortly afterward Jurong was moved to be Shannan East Circuit military governor to resist Chao, encamped at Tuanlin.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao seized Jingnan, Jurong was soon transferred to military governor of Shannan East Circuit to block him, and encamped at Tuanlin.

sentences.zh: 江西招討使曹全晸與巨容守荊門關，與賊戰，巨容偽北，巢追之，伏興林樾間，賊大敗，執賊將十三人，轉鬥一舍，虜獲不可計。

translations.literal: Jiangxi pacification commissioner Cao Quanwei and Jurong defended Jingmen Pass and fought the bandits; Jurong feigned retreat; Chao pursued; an ambush was set in the forest thickets; the bandits were greatly defeated; thirteen bandit generals were captured; they fought for one stage; captives and booty were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi pacification commissioner Cao Quanwei joined Jurong in holding Jingmen Pass. Jurong feigned a retreat, drew Huang Chao in pursuit, and sprang an ambush from the woods. The rebels were routed, thirteen of their generals were taken, and the pursuit continued for thirty li with incalculable prisoners and plunder.

sentences.zh: 巢浮江東奔，巨容追之，率十俘八，以功遷檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Chao fled east down the river; Jurong pursued; he killed eight of every ten captives; for merit he was promoted acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao fled east by river while Jurong pursued, executing eight out of every ten captives. For this service Jurong was promoted to acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲乘勝追斬巢，巨容止曰：「朝家多負人，有危難，不愛惜官賞，事平即忘之，不如留賊，為富貴作地。」

translations.literal: The generals wished to pursue the victory and behead Chao; Jurong stopped them, saying: "The court often wrongs people—when there is danger they do not spare offices and rewards, but once things are settled they forget; better to leave the bandits to make a foundation for wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to press the victory and finish off Huang Chao, but Jurong stopped them, saying, "The court is always letting people down—it hands out rank and riches in a crisis, then forgets you once the trouble passes. Better to leave the rebels alive and keep a path to fortune open.

sentences.zh: 諸將謂然，故巢復熾。

translations.literal: The generals agreed it was so; therefore Chao again flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals agreed, and so Huang Chao was able to rise again.

sentences.zh: 及陷兩京，巨容合諸道兵討之，授南面行營招討使，累兼天下兵馬先鋒開道供軍糧料使、檢校司空，封彭城縣侯。

translations.literal: When the two capitals fell, Jurong combined troops from all circuits to attack him; he was appointed southern-front pacification commissioner, repeatedly also serving as vanguard commissioner for opening roads and supplying army provisions for all troops under heaven, acting Grand Preceptor, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: After both capitals fell, Jurong gathered forces from every circuit to campaign against Huang Chao. He was appointed southern-front pacification commissioner, and in succession also served as chief vanguard commissioner for clearing roads and supplying the armies, acting Grand Preceptor, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 巨容明吏治。

translations.literal: Jurong was clear in governing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jurong was skilled at administration.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，公卿多因巨容護赴行在。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; many court officials relied on Jurong's protection to reach the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xizong was in Shu, many high officials depended on Jurong's protection to reach the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使鹿晏弘為禁軍所逐，引麾下東出襄、鄧。

translations.literal: Shannan West Circuit military governor Lu Yanhong was driven out by the imperial guard and led his followers east through Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanhong, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, was expelled by the imperial guard and marched east through Xiangzhou and Dengzhou with his troops.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權遣趙德諲合晏弘兵攻襄州，巨容不能守，奔成都。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan sent Zhao Deyin to join Yanhong's troops in attacking Xiangzhou; Jurong could not hold it and fled to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan sent Zhao Deyin to combine with Yanhong's forces and attack Xiangzhou. Jurong could not defend the city and fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 始，揚州人申屠生能化黃金，高駢客之，為呂用之所譖，亡奔襄、漢，駢遣吏捕得，生見巨容自言其術，巨容留不遣。

translations.literal: Initially Shen Tusheng of Yangzhou could transform gold; Gao Pian kept him as a guest; he was slandered by Lü Yongzhi; he fled to Xiang and Han; Pian sent officials who captured him; when brought before Jurong he explained his art; Jurong kept him and would not send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shen Tusheng of Yangzhou claimed he could transmute gold. Gao Pian took him in as a client, but Lü Yongzhi slandered him and he fled to the Xiang-Han region. Gao Pian sent officials who captured him; when he was brought before Jurong he demonstrated his technique, and Jurong kept him and refused to surrender him.

sentences.zh: 田令孜之弟遁襄州，巨容出金誇之。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi's younger brother fled to Xiangzhou; Jurong brought out gold to boast to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Lingzi's younger brother fled to Xiangzhou, Jurong flaunted gold before him.

sentences.zh: 及在蜀，匿生，使術不得傳，令孜恨之。

translations.literal: Later, in Shu, he hid Shen Tusheng so the art could not be transmitted; Lingzi hated him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while in Shu, he hid Shen Tusheng so the technique could not spread, and Tian Lingzi came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年，殺巨容，夷其宗，生並死。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longji, Jurong was killed and his clan exterminated; Shen Tusheng also died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Longji reign, Jurong was executed and his entire clan wiped out; Shen Tusheng died as well.

sentences.zh: 巨容部將馮行襲者，均州武當人，以謀勇稱裏中。

translations.literal: Jurong's subordinate general Feng Xingsi was a man of Wudang in Junzhou, famed in the district for strategy and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Among Jurong's officers was Feng Xingsi of Wudang in Junzhou, renowned locally for his cunning and bravery.

sentences.zh: 中和初，鄉豪孫喜聚眾數千人，謀攻城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, local strongman Sun Xi gathered several thousand men and plotted to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhonghe era, a local power-broker named Sun Xi raised several thousand men and planned to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 行襲伏士江隩，以單舟迎喜曰：「州人思得將軍久矣。

translations.literal: Xingsi hid soldiers at the river bend and, with a single boat, went to welcome Xi, saying: "The people of the prefecture have long wished to have a general.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingsi concealed troops along the riverbank and went out in a lone boat to greet Sun Xi, saying, "The people of this prefecture have long wanted a commander like you.

sentences.zh: 顧將軍兵多必剽掠，若留眾江北，以輕騎進，我為向導，城可下。」

translations.literal: But if the general's troops are many they will surely plunder; if you leave the multitude north of the river and advance with light cavalry, I will serve as guide—the city can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: But with a large force you are sure to loot. Leave the bulk of your men north of the river and come in with light cavalry—I will guide you, and the city will fall.

sentences.zh: 喜信之。

translations.literal: Xi believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xi believed him.

sentences.zh: 既度江，吏出迎，伏甲興，行襲擊喜，斬之，眾皆潰。

translations.literal: Once they had crossed the river, officials came out to welcome them; hidden armor rose up; Xingsi attacked Xi and beheaded him; the crowd all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After they crossed the river, officials came out to welcome them, hidden troops sprang up, and Xingsi struck down Xi and took his head. The rest of the force scattered.

sentences.zh: 行襲乘勝逐刺史呂燁，據均州，巨容因表為刺史。

translations.literal: Xingsi pressed the victory, drove out prefect Lü Ye, seized Junzhou; Jurong thereupon memorialized to make him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the victory, Xingsi pursued and expelled Prefect Lü Ye, seized control of Junzhou, and Jurong memorialized to have him appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝在蜀，均之右有長山，當襄、漢貢道，有劇賊據險劫獻物，行襲平之。

translations.literal: The emperor was in Shu; to the east of Junzhou was Mount Changshan, on the tribute route between Xiang and Han; fierce bandits held the passes and robbed tribute goods; Xingsi pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was in Shu, Mount Changshan east of Junzhou lay on the tribute road between Xiang and Han, where fierce bandits held the heights and plundered tribute. Xingsi suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 武定節度使楊守忠表為行軍司馬，使領兵搤谷口以通秦、蜀。

translations.literal: Wuding military governor Yang Shouzhong memorialized to appoint him marching commissioner and had him lead troops to choke the valley mouth and open passage between Qin and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouzhong, military governor of Wuding Circuit, recommended him as marching commissioner and sent him to hold the valley mouth and secure the route between Qin and Shu.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔李茂貞養子繼臻據金州，行襲攻拔之，昭宗即授金州防禦使。

translations.literal: Li Jizhen, foster son of Fengxiang's Li Maozhen, held Jinzhou; Xingsi attacked and captured it; Emperor Zhaozong immediately appointed him Defender of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhen, an adopted son of Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, held Jinzhou until Xingsi attacked and took it. Emperor Zhaozong promptly appointed Xingsi Defender of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時山南西道節度使楊守亮將襲京師，道金、商，行襲逆戰破之，就擢戎昭軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the time Shannan West Circuit military governor Yang Shouliang was about to raid the capital, passing through Jin and Shang; Xingsi met him in battle and defeated him; he was thereupon promoted to Rongzhao Army military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shouliang, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, marched toward the capital through Jin and Shang, Xingsi intercepted and defeated him and was immediately elevated to military governor of the Rongzhao Army.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠圍鳳翔，神策中尉韓全誨遣中人二十輩督江、淮兵過其州，行襲方附全忠，盡殺之，收詔書送全忠。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong besieged Fengxiang; Shence Army director Han Quanhui sent twenty palace eunuchs to supervise Jiang-Huai troops passing through his prefecture; Xingsi had just attached himself to Quanzhong and killed them all, seized the edicts, and sent them to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong besieged Fengxiang, Shence Army director Han Quanhui dispatched twenty palace eunuchs to oversee Jiang-Huai troops passing through Xingsi's territory. Xingsi, who had just sided with Quanzhong, slaughtered them all, seized their imperial orders, and forwarded them to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年，王建遣將王思綰攻行襲，敗其兵，州大將金行全出降，行襲奔均州。
