translations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou, Wang Jian sent general Wang Sixian to attack Xingsi, defeated his army; Jinzhou's great general Jin Xingquan came out and surrendered; Xingsi fled to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianyou, Wang Jian sent Wang Sixian against Feng Xingsi, routed his army, and Jin Xingquan, the chief general of Jinzhou, surrendered. Xingsi fled back to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 建以行全為子，更名宗朗，授觀察使，以渠、巴、開三州隸之。

translations.literal: Jian took Xingquan as his son, renamed him Zonglang, appointed him observation commissioner, and subordinated the three prefectures of Qu, Ba, and Kai to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian adopted Jin Xingquan as his son, renamed him Zonglang, made him observation commissioner, and placed the three prefectures of Qu, Ba, and Kai under his command.

sentences.zh: 宗朗不能守，焚郭邑去。

translations.literal: Zonglang could not hold them and burned the walled city as he left.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglang could not hold the territory and burned the city before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 全忠以行襲不足禦建，遣別將屯金州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong considered Xingsi insufficient to resist Jian and sent another general to garrison Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong judged that Xingsi was not strong enough to stand against Wang Jian and dispatched another general to garrison Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 行襲議徙戎昭軍於均州，以金、房為隸。

translations.literal: Xingsi proposed moving the Rongzhao Army to Junzhou, with Jin and Fang subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsi proposed relocating headquarters of the Rongzhao Army to Junzhou, with Jin and Fang prefectures placed under it.

sentences.zh: 全忠以金人不樂行襲，以馮恭領州，罷防禦使而廢戎昭軍。

translations.literal: Quanzhong, because the people of Jin did not wish to follow Xingsi, had Feng Gong lead the prefecture, abolished the Defender post, and dissolved the Rongzhao Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people of Jinzhou would not accept Xingsi, Quanzhong put Feng Gong in charge of the prefecture, abolished the defense command, and dissolved the Rongzhao Army.

sentences.zh: 趙德諲，蔡州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Deyin was a man of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Deyin was a native of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 從秦宗權為右將，以討黃巢功授申州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Qin Zongquan as right general; for merit in suppressing Huang Chao he was appointed Shenzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Qin Zongquan as a senior general and, for his achievements against Huang Chao, was appointed prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，與秦誥、鹿晏弘合兵攻襄州，節度使劉巨容奔成都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, he joined with Qin Gao and Lu Yanhong to attack Xiangzhou; military governor Liu Jurong fled to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangqi reign he combined forces with Qin Gao and Lu Yanhong to attack Xiangzhou, driving military governor Liu Jurong to flee to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 宗權假德諲山南東道節度留後，進攻荊南，悉收寶貲，留裨將王建肇守之，遺人才數百室。

translations.literal: Zongquan made Deyin acting Shannan East Circuit military governor; he advanced to attack Jingnan, collected all treasures and wealth, left deputy general Wang Jianzhao to guard it, and left behind several hundred households of people.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan appointed Deyin acting military governor of Shannan East Circuit. Deyin marched on Jingnan, seized all its valuables, left deputy general Wang Jianzhao to hold the city, and settled several hundred households there.

sentences.zh: 明年，歸州刺史郭禹來討，建肇納之，奔黔州。

translations.literal: The next year, Guizhou Prefecture governor Guo Yu came to attack; Jianzhao surrendered to him and fled to Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Guo Yu, governor of Guizhou, marched to suppress them; Wang Jianzhao submitted to him, and Deyin fled to Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德諲失荊南，又度宗權必敗，舉地附朱全忠。

translations.literal: Deyin lost Jingnan, and also anticipated that Zongquan would certainly be defeated; he surrendered all his territory to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After losing Jingnan, Deyin saw that Zongquan was doomed and surrendered his entire domain to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠方為蔡州四面行營都統，即表以自副，加忠義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was then overall commander of the encirclement forces around Cai Prefecture; he immediately submitted a memorial recommending himself as Quanzhong's deputy, and was appointed military governor of the Loyalty and Righteousness Army.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was then supreme commander of the forces encircling Cai Prefecture; Deyin at once memorialized the throne asking to serve as his deputy and was made military governor of the Loyalty and Righteousness Army.

sentences.zh: 宗權平，加中書令，封淮安郡王，卒。

translations.literal: When Zongquan was pacified, he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Huai'an Commandery, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zongquan was suppressed, Deyin was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Huai'an, and died.

sentences.zh: 子匡凝嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kuangning succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuangning inherited his position.

sentences.zh: 匡凝，字光儀，由唐州刺史自為山南東道節度留後，昭宗即授節度使，不三年，以威惠聞。

translations.literal: Kuangning, courtesy name Guangyi, from the post of Tangzhou prefect appointed himself acting military governor of Shannan East Circuit; Emperor Zhaozong then conferred upon him the title of military governor; within less than three years, he became known for authority and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning, styled Guangyi, had risen from Tangzhou prefect to declare himself acting military governor of Shannan East Circuit; Emperor Zhaozong then confirmed him as full governor, and in less than three years he won renown for combining stern authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校太尉兼中書令。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to honorary Grand General and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to Honorary Grand General and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 匡凝矜嚴盛飾，前後持鑒自照。

translations.literal: Kuangning was haughty and stern, overly ornate in dress; morning and evening he held a mirror to examine himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning was proud, severe, and fond of elaborate dress; morning and night he carried a mirror to inspect his appearance.

sentences.zh: 全忠之敗清口，匡凝與奉國節度使崔洪、河東李克用、淮南楊行密約合兵攻全忠。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong was defeated at Qingkou, Kuangning together with Fengguo military governor Cui Hong, Hedong's Li Keyong, and Huainan's Yang Xingmi agreed to join forces and attack Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Quanzhong's defeat at Qingkou, Kuangning joined Fengguo governor Cui Hong, Li Keyong of Hedong, and Yang Xingmi of Huainan in a pact to combine armies and strike Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 會方城鎮遏使度軫奔全忠，發其謀。

translations.literal: At that time Fangcheng garrison commissioner Du Zhen fled to Quanzhong and exposed their plot.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Du Zhen, garrison commissioner of Fangcheng, defected to Quanzhong and revealed the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 全忠移書切責，使氏叔琮攻唐州，刺史趙匡璠降。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent a stern rebuking letter and dispatched Shi Shuzong to attack Tang Prefecture; prefect Zhao Kuangfan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong wrote a harsh letter of reproach and sent Shi Shuzong against Tang Prefecture; its prefect Zhao Kuangfan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進圍隋州，執刺史趙匡璘，斬首五千級；

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Suizhou, captured prefect Zhao Kuanglin, and beheaded five thousand enemy soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Shi then pressed on to besiege Suizhou, seized its prefect Zhao Kuanglin, and took five thousand heads;

sentences.zh: 拔鄧州，執刺史國湘。

translations.literal: He captured Deng Prefecture and seized prefect Guo Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: he also took Deng Prefecture and captured its prefect Guo Xiang.

sentences.zh: 匡凝懼，乞盟。

translations.literal: Kuangning was afraid and requested a treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning, alarmed, begged for peace.

sentences.zh: 全忠使親將陳俊、王紳入叔琮軍，崔洪留之，紳亡歸。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent his trusted generals Chen Jun and Wang Shen into Shuzong's army; Cui Hong detained them, and Shen fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent his close generals Chen Jun and Wang Shen into Shuzong's camp; Cui Hong held them, but Shen escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 洪與行密欲邀友恭軍，不克。

translations.literal: Hong and Xingmi wanted to intercept Li Yougong's army but failed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Xingmi tried to ambush Li Yougong's army but could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 會河東客伊超使淮南還，過蔡，洪亦留之，因是並俊送全忠，以部將苛拘為解，遣兄賢入質，全忠還之，質洪子於汴。

translations.literal: When Hedong envoy Yi Chao, returning from a mission to Huainan, passed through Cai, Hong also detained him; thereby he sent Jun together to Quanzhong, using harsh detention of his subordinate officers as explanation, sent his elder brother Xian as hostage; Quanzhong returned Xian, and took Hong's son as hostage at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Chao, a Hedong envoy returning from Huainan, passed through Cai, Hong detained him as well; he then released Jun and sent him to Quanzhong, citing the harsh imprisonment of his officers as justification, and dispatched his elder brother Xian as a hostage. Quanzhong sent Xian back but kept Hong's son at Bian as a pledge.

sentences.zh: 全忠使賢調蔡卒二千出戍。

translations.literal: Quanzhong had Xian muster two thousand Cai troops to go out on garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ordered Xian to levy two thousand Cai soldiers for garrison duty elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 將行，大將崔景思不悅，殺賢，洪懼，驅民趨申州，遂奔行密，麾鼓亙百餘里。

translations.literal: As they were about to depart, great general Cui Jingsi was displeased and killed Xian; Hong was afraid, drove the people toward Shen Prefecture, then fled to Xingmi, with banners and drums stretching over a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Just before they set out, the senior officer Cui Jingsi, resentful, killed Xian. Hong, terrified, drove the populace toward Shen Prefecture and then fled to Xingmi, his banners and drums trailing for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 武昌杜洪邀之，弗及，蔡士多亡去，從者才二千人。

translations.literal: Wuchang's Du Hong tried to intercept him but did not reach him in time; many Cai soldiers fled away, and his followers numbered only two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong of Wuchang tried to cut him off but arrived too late; most of the Cai troops scattered, and only two thousand men followed him.

sentences.zh: 全忠以其兵分可圖也，乃使楊師厚攻匡凝，自將中軍繼之，屯臨漢。

translations.literal: Quanzhong, thinking that since Hong's army was divided it could be seized upon, then sent Yang Shihou to attack Kuangning, personally leading the central army to follow, and encamped at Linhan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong judged that Hong's forces were now split and vulnerable, so he sent Yang Shihou against Kuangning while he himself led the main army after him and encamped at Linhan.

sentences.zh: 匡凝遣客謝，囚不遣，敗荊南救兵，俘其將。

translations.literal: Kuangning sent an emissary to apologize; Quanzhong imprisoned him and would not release him, defeated Jingnan relief troops, and captured their general.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning sent an envoy to apologize, but Quanzhong imprisoned the man and refused to let him go; he then routed Jingnan's relief force and captured one of its generals.

sentences.zh: 全忠循江而南，師厚繇陰谷伐木為梁。

translations.literal: Quanzhong followed the river southward; Shihou cut timber in a hidden valley to build a bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong marched south along the river while Shihou felled trees in a secluded ravine to construct a bridge.

sentences.zh: 匡凝以兵二萬瀕江戰，大敗，乃燔州，單舸夜奔揚州。

translations.literal: Kuangning fought with twenty thousand troops along the riverbank, suffered a great defeat, then burned the prefectural seat, and fled alone by boat at night to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning gave battle with twenty thousand men along the river, was thoroughly defeated, burned the prefectural seat, and fled alone by boat at night to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密見之曰：「君在鎮，輕車重馬輸於賊，今敗乃歸我邪？」

translations.literal: Xingmi saw him and said: "When you were in command of your territory, you sent light wagons and heavy horses with supplies to the bandits—now that you are defeated you come to me?
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi saw him he said, "While you held your command, you sent light carts and heavy horses laden with supplies to the enemy—and now, after defeat, you come to me?

sentences.zh: 筠自殺。

translations.literal: Yun committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning took his own life.

sentences.zh: 全忠以師厚為山南東道節度留後，遂趨江陵。

translations.literal: Quanzhong appointed Shihou as acting military governor of Shannan East Circuit, then hurried toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong made Shihou acting governor of Shannan East Circuit and then pressed on toward Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 匡明亦謀奔淮南，子承規諫曰：「昔諸葛兄弟分仕二國，若適揚州，是自取疑也。」

translations.literal: Kuangming also planned to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui remonstrated, saying: "In ancient times the Zhuge brothers served in two different states—if we go to Yangzhou, we would be inviting suspicion upon ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming also planned to flee to Huainan, but his son Chenggui admonished him: "Long ago the Zhuge brothers served rival states; if we go to Yangzhou, we will only invite suspicion upon ourselves.

sentences.zh: 匡明謂然，乃趨成都，王建待以賓禮，授武信軍節度使，分其眾為崇義、勇義、順義、廣義四都，全忠遂有荊南。

translations.literal: Kuangming agreed this was so, then went to Chengdu; Wang Jian treated him with guest ritual, appointed him military governor of Wuxin Army, divided his followers into four commands—Chongyi, Yongyi, Shunyi, and Guangyi—and Quanzhong thereby gained Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming agreed, turned instead toward Chengdu, and was received by Wang Jian with the honors due a guest and made military governor of the Wuxin Army; Wang divided his followers into four commands—Chongyi, Yongyi, Shunyi, and Guangyi—and Quanzhong thereby took possession of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 楊守亮，曹州人，本姓訾，名亮。

translations.literal: Yang Shouliang was a native of Caozhou; his original surname was Zi and his given name was Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouliang came from Caozhou; his original surname was Zi and his given name was Liang.

sentences.zh: 與弟信俱從王仙芝為盜。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Xin both followed Wang Xianzhi as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Xin both joined Wang Xianzhi as brigands.

sentences.zh: 亮身長七尺餘，色如鐵。

translations.literal: Liang was over seven chi tall, his complexion like iron.
translations.idiomatic: Liang stood more than seven chi in height, with a complexion dark as iron.

sentences.zh: 仙芝死，又事徐唐莒，劫剽洪、饒二州。

translations.literal: After Xianzhi died, he again served Xu Tangju, raiding and plundering Hong and Rao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhi's death he served Xu Tangju and raided Hong and Rao prefectures.

sentences.zh: 楊復光平江西，得其兄弟，養為假子，以信養於弟復恭家，曰守亮、守信。

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang pacified Jiangxi, captured the brothers, and adopted them as foster sons; Xin was raised in his younger brother Fugong's household—they were called Shouliang and Shouxin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Fuguang pacified Jiangxi he captured the brothers and adopted them as foster sons; Xin was raised in Fuguang's younger brother Fugong's household, and they were renamed Shouliang and Shouxin.

sentences.zh: 復恭收京師。

translations.literal: Fugong recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong then recovered the capital.

sentences.zh: 守亮以戰多，拜山南西道節度使、檢校太保，守信興平軍節度使，並同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Shouliang for his many battles was appointed military governor of Shannan West Circuit and honorary Grand Protector; Shouxin was appointed military governor of Xingping Army—both as concurrent co-chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: For his many campaigns Shouliang was made military governor of Shannan West Circuit and Honorary Grand Protector, while Shouxin was made governor of the Xingping Army; both also served as co-chancellors.

sentences.zh: 復恭又以假子守貞為龍劍節度使，守忠為武定軍節度使，守厚為綿州刺史。

translations.literal: Fugong also made his foster sons Shouzhen military governor of Longjian Army, Shouzhong military governor of Wuding Army, and Shouhou prefect of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong further appointed his foster sons Shouzhen governor of the Longjian Army, Shouzhong governor of the Wuding Army, and Shouhou prefect of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，朱玫取興、鳳州，虢州刺史滿存以兵赴行在，復收二州，昭宗擢為感義軍節度使，累檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事，與復恭四假子及利閬觀察使席儔等共攻王建。

translations.literal: Initially, Zhu Mei captured Xing and Feng prefectures; Guozhou prefect Man Cun led troops to the mobile court, recovered both prefectures; Emperor Zhaozong promoted him to military governor of Ganyi Army, repeatedly to honorary Minister of Works and co-chancellor; together with Fugong's four foster sons and Lichuan observation commissioner Xi Chou and others they jointly attacked Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhu Mei seized Xing and Feng prefectures, Man Cun, prefect of Guo, marched with troops to the emperor's camp and recovered both prefectures; Emperor Zhaozong promoted him to military governor of the Ganyi Army and eventually to Honorary Minister of Works and co-chancellor. Together with Fugong's four foster sons and Xi Chou, observation commissioner of Lichuan, he joined in an attack on Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 建軍已圍楊晟，分軍逼守厚，軍未成列而敗。

translations.literal: Jian's army had already besieged Yang Sheng; he divided his army to press Shouhou—the army had not formed ranks when they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's army was already besieging Yang Sheng when he detached a force to pressure Shouhou; the troops had not even formed ranks before they were beaten.

sentences.zh: 先是，守貞、守忠聞建兵出，拔眾奔綿州，並力共攻東川，弗勝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shouzhen and Shouzhong, hearing that Jian's troops had marched out, withdrew their forces and fled to Mianzhou; combining strength they jointly attacked Dongchuan but did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Shouzhen and Shouzhong heard that Wang Jian's army had marched out, they pulled back their forces and fled to Mianzhou; joining together they attacked Dongchuan but failed to win.

sentences.zh: 建將華洪以兵萬人壁綿州之郊，敗守忠、守厚，二人分道行，收兵趨閬州。

translations.literal: Jian's general Hua Hong with ten thousand troops encamped on the outskirts of Mianzhou, defeated Shouzhong and Shouhou; the two men traveled by separate routes, gathered their troops, and headed for Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's general Hua Hong encamped with ten thousand men on the outskirts of Mianzhou, defeated Shouzhong and Shouhou, and the two men split up, regrouped their soldiers, and made for Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始，復恭敗，依守亮。

translations.literal: At first, after Fugong was defeated, he relied on Shouliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Fugong was first defeated, he depended on Shouliang.

sentences.zh: 而鳳翔李茂貞、邠寧王行瑜、鎮國韓建等共劾守亮納叛人，請以鎮兵討之。

translations.literal: Then Fengxiang's Li Maozhen, Binning's Wang Xingyu, Zhenguo's Han Jian and others jointly impeached Shouliang for harboring rebels, requesting that garrison troops be sent to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Binning, Han Jian of Zhenguo, and others jointly accused Shouliang of sheltering rebels and asked that frontier troops be sent to punish him.

sentences.zh: 茂貞自為興元節度使，以書誚責宰相。

translations.literal: Maozhen appointed himself military governor of Xingyuan and sent a letter reproaching the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen declared himself military governor of Xingyuan and sent a letter rebuking the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 帝為削守亮官爵，因詔茂貞問罪。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stripped Shouliang of his offices and ranks, and issued an edict for Maozhen to inquire into his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon stripped Shouliang of rank and title and issued an edict commissioning Maozhen to investigate and punish him.

sentences.zh: 滿存來救不克，以眾入興元。

translations.literal: Man Cun came to rescue but failed, and led his army into Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Man Cun came to relieve him but could not break through, and entered Xingyuan with his army.

sentences.zh: 茂貞拔興、鳳、洋三州，破守亮於西，乘勝入興元。

translations.literal: Maozhen captured Xing, Feng, and Yang prefectures, defeated Shouliang in the west, and following up his victory entered Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen took Xing, Feng, and Yang prefectures, defeated Shouliang in the west, and following up his victory entered Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 復恭挾諸假子及存奔閬州。

translations.literal: Fugong took along all the foster sons and Cun and fled to Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong fled to Lang Prefecture, taking all his foster sons and Man Cun with him.

sentences.zh: 洪進圍之。

translations.literal: Hong advanced to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Hong pressed forward and besieged them there.

sentences.zh: 帝以徐彥若帥鳳翔，以興元授茂貞。

translations.literal: The emperor put Xu Yanruo in command of Fengxiang and granted Xingyuan to Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Xu Yanruo commander of Fengxiang and awarded Xingyuan to Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 茂貞不肯拜，帝乃以其子繼密為興元節度使。

translations.literal: Maozhen refused to accept the appointment, and the emperor thereupon made his son Jimi military governor of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen refused to accept the post, so the emperor appointed his son Jimi military governor of Xingyuan instead.

sentences.zh: 俄而洪拔閬州，守亮等皆挺身走，將北奔太原，趨商山，饑甚，丐食於野，為邏戍所縛，見韓建，守亮視建左右八百人皆常隸己，語建曰：「此屬吾養之素厚，無一為我死。

translations.literal: Before long Hong captured Lang Prefecture; Shouliang and the others all fled for their lives, intending to flee north to Taiyuan and heading toward Shangshan. Greatly starving, they begged for food in the wilds, were bound by border garrison troops, and were brought before Han Jian. Shouliang saw that the eight hundred men at Jian's side had all formerly served under him, and said to Jian: "These men I always treated with great generosity—yet not one would die for me.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hua Hong took Lang Prefecture, and Shouliang and his party fled for their lives, intending to escape north to Taiyuan by way of Shangshan. Half starved, they begged food in the countryside, were seized by frontier guards, and brought before Han Jian. Shouliang saw that the eight hundred men around Jian had all once been his own troops, and said to him: "I always treated these men well, yet not one of them would die for me.

sentences.zh: 公無費衣食，不如殺之。」

translations.literal: My lord, do not waste food and clothing on them—better to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: My lord, do not waste food and clothing on them—you might as well kill them.

sentences.zh: 建許諾。

translations.literal: Jian agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian consented.

sentences.zh: 復曰：「公幸貸我，俾生見天子，陳先人功，萬有一不死。」

translations.literal: He added: "My lord, I beg you spare me, that I may live to see the Son of Heaven, set forth my forebears' achievements, and perhaps in ten thousand cases not die.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "My lord, please spare me so I may live to see the emperor, recount my forebears' service, and perhaps—against all odds—survive.

sentences.zh: 建檻車送京師，吏縛以帛，內球於口。

translations.literal: Jian sent him in a caged cart to the capital; officials bound him with silk and put a ball in his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent him to the capital in a prison cart; officials bound him with cloth and stuffed a ball into his mouth.

sentences.zh: 帝禦延喜樓問反狀，守亮不得語，頷而已。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the Yanxi Tower to question him about the rebellion; Shouliang could not speak and could only nod.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went up to the Yanxi Tower to question him about the revolt; Shouliang could not speak and could only nod.

sentences.zh: 左右白服罪，即執獻太廟，斬獨柳下，梟於市。

translations.literal: His attendants declared his confession of guilt; he was seized, presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, beheaded beneath the Lone Willow, and his head was displayed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants reported that he had confessed; he was seized, offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, beheaded beneath the Lone Willow, and his head was displayed in the market.

sentences.zh: 守厚死巴州，麾下兵多歸王建。

translations.literal: Shouhou died at Ba Prefecture; most of the soldiers under his command went over to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Shouhou died at Ba Prefecture, and most of his troops went over to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 存奔京師，為左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Cun fled to the capital and was made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Man Cun fled to the capital and was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 楊晟，不詳宗系。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng; his lineage is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng—his family background is unknown.

sentences.zh: 隸鳳翔軍，節度使李昌符畏其勇，欲殺之，妾周擿使亡去，隸神策軍為都校。

translations.literal: He served in the Fengxiang army. Military governor Li Changfu feared his courage and wished to kill him; his concubine Zhou Li helped him escape, and he joined the Shence Army as a regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Fengxiang army. Governor Li Changfu feared his bravery and wanted him killed, but concubine Zhou Li helped him flee; he then entered the Shence Army as a regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 僖宗在陳倉，邠寧朱玫遣萬騎合昌符追行在，乃擢晟感義軍節度使、檢校司空，守大散關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong was at Chencang, Zhu Mei of Binning sent ten thousand horsemen to join Changfu in pursuing the imperial procession; Sheng was then promoted to military governor of the Ganyi Army and Honorary Minister of Works and stationed at Dasan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xizong was at Chencang, Zhu Mei of Binning sent ten thousand cavalry to join Changfu in pursuing the court; Sheng was then made military governor of the Ganyi Army and Honorary Minister of Works and ordered to hold Dasan Pass.

sentences.zh: 玫兵攻關，晟數卻，戰潘氏，遂大敗，內外無固誌。

translations.literal: Mei's troops attacked the pass; Sheng repelled them several times, but at Panshi was utterly defeated, and inside and outside there was no firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Mei's army assaulted the pass; Sheng beat them back several times, but at Panshi he suffered a crushing defeat and morale collapsed throughout the camp.

sentences.zh: 帝更徙興元，晟西奔，玫取興、鳳二州。

translations.literal: The emperor moved again to Xingyuan; Sheng fled west, and Mei took Xing and Feng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moved on to Xingyuan; Sheng fled westward, and Mei seized Xing and Feng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 晟襲文州，逐刺史，據成、龍、茂等州。

translations.literal: Sheng raided Wen Prefecture, expelled the prefect, and held Cheng, Long, Mao, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng attacked Wen Prefecture, drove out its prefect, and seized Cheng, Long, Mao, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 王建攻成都，田令孜以晟故將，與連和，假威戎軍節度使，守彭州。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian attacked Chengdu, Tian Lingzi, since Sheng was a former general of his, allied with him, made him acting military governor of the Weirong Army, and stationed him at Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian besieged Chengdu, Tian Lingzi—Sheng having been one of his old commanders—joined forces with him, made him acting governor of the Weirong Army, and posted him at Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晟擊建，無功引還。

translations.literal: Sheng attacked Jian, achieved nothing, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng attacked Jian but won nothing and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 且畏建圖己，乃約山南西道節度使楊守亮兄弟合謀拒建，掠新繁，焚漢州，又攻東川顧彥暉，為建兵所逐。

translations.literal: Moreover fearing that Jian plotted against him, he joined Yang Shouliang, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, and his brothers in a conspiracy to resist Jian—plundered Xinfan, burned Han Prefecture, and also attacked Gu Yanhui of Dongchuan, but was driven off by Jian's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Jian meant to destroy him, he conspired with Yang Shouliang, governor of Shannan West Circuit, and his brothers to resist Jian: they raided Xinfan, burned Han Prefecture, and also attacked Gu Yanhui of Dongchuan, but were driven off by Jian's army.

sentences.zh: 建使王宗裕率騎五萬圍晟，食四郊麥，掠民資產。

translations.literal: Jian sent Wang Zongyu with fifty thousand horsemen to besiege Sheng; they ate the wheat of the four suburbs and plundered the people's property.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent Wang Zongyu with fifty thousand cavalry to besiege Sheng; the army lived off the suburban wheat harvest and looted the people's goods.

sentences.zh: 晟假子實以騎八千降於建，建以奇兵襲楊守厚等，皆亡去。

translations.literal: Sheng's foster son Shi surrendered to Jian with eight thousand horsemen; Jian sent a surprise force against Yang Shouhou and the others, and all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's foster son Shi defected to Jian with eight thousand horsemen; Jian then sent a surprise force against Yang Shouhou and the others, and they all fled.

sentences.zh: 晟開門決戰，大敗，遂約降。

translations.literal: Sheng opened the gates for a decisive battle, was utterly defeated, and then agreed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng opened the gates for a final battle, was routed, and then agreed to surrender.

sentences.zh: 建饋十羊，晟曰：「以我為機上肉乎？」

translations.literal: Jian sent ten sheep as a gift; Sheng said: "Do you take me for meat on the chopping block?
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent him ten sheep; Sheng said, "Do you take me for meat on the block?

sentences.zh: 不出。

translations.literal: He did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 建築甬道屬陴以入，斬晟首。

translations.literal: Jian built a covered corridor connecting to the wall and entered; he cut off Sheng's head.
translations.idiomatic: Jian built a covered corridor up to the wall, entered the city, and cut off Sheng's head.

sentences.zh: 晟有仁心，下懷其恩，雖城中食盡，無叛者。

translations.literal: Sheng had a benevolent heart; the lower ranks cherished his kindness, and though food in the city was exhausted, there were no defectors.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was humane at heart, and his men cherished his kindness; though the city ran out of food, none betrayed him.

sentences.zh: 初，昌符死，晟得其妾周，母事之，周請為妻，晟固辭，旦夕問省，乃視事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Changfu died, Sheng obtained his concubine Zhou, treated her as a mother; Zhou asked to become his wife, but Sheng firmly declined, inquiring after her morning and evening before attending to business.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Changfu's death, Sheng took his concubine Zhou and treated her like a mother; though Zhou asked to marry him, he steadfastly refused, attending to her morning and evening before handling affairs.

sentences.zh: 愛將安師建者，勇而有禮，既就執，建顧曰：「爾報楊司徒足矣，能從我乎？」

translations.literal: His beloved general An Shijian was brave and courteous; once captured, Jian said to him: "You have already repaid Minister Yang—will you follow me?
translations.idiomatic: His favorite commander An Shijian was brave and courteous; once captured, Jian said to him, "You have already repaid Minister Yang—is that enough, or will you follow me?

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「司徒誓同死生，不忍復戴日月。」

translations.literal: He replied in thanks: "The Minister swore we would live and die together—I cannot bear to serve another master under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Minister and I swore to live and die together—I cannot bear to serve another lord under heaven.

sentences.zh: 三謂不回，乃戮之。

translations.literal: After three times asking with no change of heart, Jian executed him.
translations.idiomatic: After asking three times without success, Jian had him killed.

sentences.zh: 顧彥朗、彥暉者，豐州人，並為天德軍小校。

translations.literal: Gu Yanlang and Yanhui were natives of Feng Prefecture; both served as junior officers in the Tiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanlang and Gu Yanhui were from Feng Prefecture; both served as junior officers in the Tiande Army.

sentences.zh: 其使蔡京以兄弟有封侯相，每厚禮之，使子贈賚，稍稍進秩。

translations.literal: Their envoy Cai Jing, because the brothers had the makings of enfeoffment and chancellorship, always treated them generously, sent his son with gifts, and gradually promoted their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoy Cai Jing, seeing that the brothers had the makings of marquis and chancellor, always treated them well, sent his son with gifts, and gradually raised their rank.

sentences.zh: 黃巢亂長安，率軍同復京師。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao ravaged Chang'an, they led troops together to recover the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao threw Chang'an into chaos, they led troops together to recover the capital.

sentences.zh: 彥朗遷累右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Yanlang was promoted in succession to Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang rose through successive promotions to Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，擢拜東川節度使、檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: During Guangqi, he was elevated to military governor of Dongchuan, Honorary Grand Mentor, and co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangqi era he was appointed military governor of Dongchuan, Honorary Grand Mentor, and co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 至劍門，陳敬瑄吏奪其節，彥朗不得入，保利州。

translations.literal: When he reached Jianmen, Chen Jingxuan's officials seized his insignia of office; Yanlang could not enter and held Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianmen, officials of Chen Jingxuan seized his commission; Yanlang could not enter the circuit and held Li Prefecture instead.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄誣劾彥朗擅興兵掠西境。

translations.literal: Jingxuan falsely accused Yanlang of raising troops without authorization and raiding the western border.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan falsely impeached Yanlang for raising troops on his own authority and raiding the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 僖宗下詔申曉講和，乃得到軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong issued an edict explaining and calling for peace, and only then was he able to reach his army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong issued an edict clarifying the situation and calling for reconciliation, and only then was Yanlang able to join his army.

sentences.zh: 署彥暉漢州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Yanhui prefect of Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yanhui prefect of Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，楊守亮忌壁州刺史王建兇暴，欲逐之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Shouliang resented Wang Jian, prefect of Bi Prefecture, for his violence and cruelty and wished to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Shouliang resented Bi Prefecture governor Wang Jian for his brutality and wanted to expel him.

sentences.zh: 建聞，合溪洞豪酋取閬州，擊利州，刺史走，即據二州，守亮不能制。

translations.literal: Jian heard of this and allied with powerful chiefs of the stream-and-cave regions to seize Lang Prefecture and attack Li Prefecture; the prefect fled, and he immediately held both prefectures; Shouliang could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian heard of this, he joined stream-and-cave chieftains to take Lang Prefecture and attack Li Prefecture; the prefect fled, and he immediately held both prefectures, beyond Shouliang's control.

sentences.zh: 彥朗與建雅舊，陰助貲饟。

translations.literal: Yanlang and Jian had been old friends; he secretly supplied funds and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang and Jian were old friends, and Yanlang secretly supplied him with money and provisions.

sentences.zh: 建攻成都，彥朗挾故憾，與並力，道路鄣梗。

translations.literal: When Jian attacked Chengdu, Yanlang, nursing an old grudge, joined forces with him, and the roads were blocked with barriers.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian marched on Chengdu, Yanlang, still smarting from old grievances, joined him in the campaign and blocked the roads.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄告難於朝，帝詔和解，又敕李茂貞鐫諭。

translations.literal: Jingxuan reported his peril to the court; the emperor ordered reconciliation and also commanded Li Maozhen to inscribe and proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan appealed to the court for help; the emperor ordered a settlement and also commanded Li Maozhen to circulate the edict.

sentences.zh: 會彥朗卒，彥暉自知留後。

translations.literal: When Yanlang died, Yanhui appointed himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanlang died, Yanhui declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 明年為節度使。

translations.literal: The next year he became military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 中人送節，為綿州刺史楊守厚所留。

translations.literal: When a eunuch came bearing the insignia of office, he was detained by Yang Shouhou, prefect of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch arrived bearing the commission, Yang Shouhou, prefect of Mian Prefecture, detained him.

sentences.zh: 守厚發兵攻梓州，彥暉告急於建，建使李簡救之，戒曰：「賊破，並取彥暉，無須再往也。」

translations.literal: Shouhou mobilized troops to attack Zizhou; Yanhui urgently appealed to Jian, who sent Li Jian to the rescue with the warning: "When the enemy is broken, seize Yanhui as well—no need to go back again.
translations.idiomatic: Shouhou raised troops to attack Zizhou; Yanhui urgently appealed to Jian, who sent Li Jian to relieve him with the instruction, "Once the enemy is broken, take Yanhui too—do not come back empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 簡破守厚軍，彥暉辭疾，不克取。

translations.literal: Li Jian defeated Shouhou's army; Yanhui pleaded illness and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian routed Shouhou's army, but Yanhui pleaded illness and could not be seized.

sentences.zh: 建素有吞噬心，以彥朗與婚婭，久未忍。

translations.literal: Jian had long harbored ambitions of swallowing up neighboring territories; because Yanlang was related by marriage, he had long restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had long wanted to swallow neighboring territory, but because Yanlang was connected by marriage he had held back for years.

sentences.zh: 及彥暉，則交好愈疏，而境上關賦相稽詬，建怒。

translations.literal: As for Yanhui, their friendship grew ever more distant, and border tolls and levies became subjects of mutual recrimination; Jian grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: With Yanhui, however, relations grew steadily worse; border tolls and levies became grounds for mutual accusations, and Jian grew angry.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，遂攻彥暉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingfu he attacked Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingfu he attacked Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 彥暉請救於楊守亮，遣楊子彥戍梓，執建大將王宗弼，彥暉責曰：「王公何以見討？

translations.literal: Yanhui appealed to Yang Shouliang for aid and sent Yang Ziyan to garrison Zizhou; he captured Jian's general Wang Zongbi; Yanhui reproached him: "Why has Lord Wang come to attack me?
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui appealed to Yang Shouliang for help and sent Yang Ziyan to garrison Zizhou; he captured Jian's general Wang Zongbi and rebuked him, "Why has Lord Wang come to attack me?

sentences.zh: 君為大將，不諫雲何？」

translations.literal: As a senior commander, why did you not remonstrate with him?
translations.idiomatic: You are a senior commander—why did you not remonstrate with him?

sentences.zh: 宗弼謝罪，即解縛，使就館，帟幕衾服皆具，更養為子，改名琛。

translations.literal: Zongbi apologized; he was immediately unbound, lodged as a guest with curtains, bedding, and clothing all provided, and was adopted as a son, renamed Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi apologized; Yanhui immediately freed him, lodged him as a guest with full furnishings, adopted him as a son, and renamed him Chen.

sentences.zh: 明年，建將華洪破綿州，守厚走，得彥暉節。

translations.literal: The next year, Jian's general Hua Hong captured Mian Prefecture; Shouhou fled, and he obtained Yanhui's insignia of office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jian's general Hua Hong took Mian Prefecture; Shouhou fled, and Jian seized Yanhui's commission.

sentences.zh: 時詔已進彥暉檢校司空、東川節度使矣。

translations.literal: By then an edict had already promoted Yanhui to Honorary Minister of Works and military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had already promoted Yanhui to Honorary Minister of Works and military governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，昭宗在石門，督彥暉、建赴行在。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning, Emperor Zhaozong was at Shimen and ordered Yanhui and Jian to proceed to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianning, Emperor Zhaozong was at Shimen and ordered Yanhui and Jian to come to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 建率兵二十萬次綿州，即劾彥暉劫輜運，回襲之。

translations.literal: Jian led two hundred thousand troops to encamp at Mian Prefecture; he immediately accused Yanhui of robbing supply convoys and turned back to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian led two hundred thousand men to encamp at Mian Prefecture, then accused Yanhui of seizing supply trains and turned back to attack him.

sentences.zh: 彥暉不敢出，但遣人塞建舟路，建遂擊取巴、閬、蓬、渠、通、果、龍、利八州。

translations.literal: Yanhui dared not sally forth but only sent men to block Jian's river routes; Jian then seized the eight prefectures of Ba, Lang, Peng, Qu, Tong, Guo, Long, and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui dared not come out but only sent men to block Jian's river routes; Jian then seized Ba, Lang, Peng, Qu, Tong, Guo, Long, and Li—eight prefectures in all.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人為兩川宣諭協和使。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched a eunuch as envoy to announce reconciliation between the Two Chuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch as envoy to proclaim reconciliation between the Two Chuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 建奉詔還，而兵不解。

translations.literal: Jian accepted the edict and returned, but his troops did not disband.
translations.idiomatic: Jian accepted the edict and withdrew, but his army did not stand down.

sentences.zh: 彥暉謀窘，因大略漢、眉、資、簡等州。

translations.literal: Yanhui, hard pressed in his planning, thereupon broadly raided Han, Mei, Zi, Jian, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, Yanhui thereupon launched wide-ranging raids on Han, Mei, Zi, Jian, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞亦欲爭其地，使子興元節度使繼密引軍救彥暉，以窺東川。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen also wished to seize the territory; he sent his son Jimi, military governor of Xingyuan, to lead troops to rescue Yanhui, intending to probe Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen also wanted the territory; he sent his son Jimi, governor of Xingyuan, to march to Yanhui's relief and probe Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，華洪率眾五萬攻彥暉，取渝、昌、普三州，壁梓州南，敗彥暉兵，奪鎧馬八百，凡五十戰，圍遂固。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Hua Hong led fifty thousand men against Yanhui, took Yu, Chang, and Pu prefectures, encamped south of Zizhou, defeated Yanhui's army, seized eight hundred sets of armor and horses; after fifty battles the siege was firmly set.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Hua Hong led fifty thousand men against Yanhui, took Yu, Chang, and Pu prefectures, encamped south of Zizhou, defeated Yanhui's forces, and captured eight hundred sets of armor and horses; after fifty engagements the siege tightened.

sentences.zh: 帝仍遣左諫議大夫李洵諭止，建拒命。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Left Remonstrance Counselor Li Xun to command a halt; Jian refused the order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Left Remonstrance Counselor Li Xun to order a halt; Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 帝以嗣郯王戒丕鎮鳳翔，徙茂貞代建，皆不奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Heir Apparent Prince of Tancheng Jiepi to garrison Fengxiang and transferred Maozhen to replace Jian; none obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Heir Apparent Prince of Tancheng Jiepi to hold Fengxiang and ordered Maozhen to replace Jian; none obeyed.

sentences.zh: 梓有鏡堂，世稱其麗，彥暉嘗會諸將堂上，養子瑤尤親信，彥暉以所佩劍號「疥癆賓」佩之，使侍左右。

translations.literal: Zizhou had a Mirror Hall renowned for its beauty; Yanhui once gathered his generals in the hall; his adopted son Yao was especially trusted; Yanhui gave him the sword he wore, named "Guest of Scabies and Consumption," to wear and attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhou had a Mirror Hall famed for its splendor; Yanhui once entertained his generals there. His adopted son Yao was especially close to him; Yanhui gave Yao the sword he wore, called "Jielao Guest," to wear and keep at his side.

sentences.zh: 嘗語諸將曰：「與公等生死同之，違者先齒『疥癆賓』！」

translations.literal: He once told the generals: "I share life and death with you all—whoever violates this will first taste 'Guest of Scabies and Consumption'!
translations.idiomatic: He once told his generals, "I live and die with you all—whoever breaks faith will first taste 'Jielao Guest'!

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The assembly replied: "Aye.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Aye.

sentences.zh: 及圍急，瑤請聚親信飲，得同死。

translations.literal: When the siege grew critical, Yao asked to gather trusted men for a drink so they might die together.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege tightened, Yao asked to gather his trusted men for a final drink so they could die together.

sentences.zh: 彥暉顧王琛曰：「爾非我舊，可自求生。」

translations.literal: Yanhui turned to Wang Chen and said: "You are not one of my old followers—you may seek to save yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui turned to Wang Chen and said, "You are not one of my old men—you may save yourself.

sentences.zh: 指頹垣令逸。

translations.literal: He pointed to a ruined wall and told him to escape.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to a crumbling wall and told him to flee.

sentences.zh: 彥暉手殺妻子，乃自刎，宗族諸將皆死，麾下兵猶七萬。

translations.literal: Yanhui personally killed his wife and children, then cut his own throat; his clansmen and generals all died; his troops still numbered seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui killed his wife and children with his own hand, then cut his throat; his kinsmen and generals all died, though his army still numbered seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 初，韋昭度為招討使，彥暉、建皆為大校。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei Zhaodu was pacification commissioner, Yanhui and Jian were both senior commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wei Zhaodu served as pacification commissioner, Yanhui and Jian were both senior commanders under him.

sentences.zh: 彥暉詳緩有儒者風，建左右髡發黥面若鬼，見者皆笑。

translations.literal: Yanhui was deliberate and unhurried with the bearing of a scholar; Jian's attendants were shorn and tattooed on the face like demons, and all who saw them laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was calm and measured, with the air of a scholar; Jian's attendants were shorn and tattooed like demons, and everyone who saw them laughed.

sentences.zh: 至是錄笑者皆殺之。

translations.literal: At this point he registered those who had laughed and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Now he recorded the names of those who had laughed and had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 私署洪為東川節度留後。

translations.literal: He privately appointed Hong acting military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He privately appointed Hua Hong acting military governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《詩》雲「戎狄是膺，荊舒是懲」，嫉其為中國之害也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Book of Odes says, "Assail the Rong and Di, punish Jing and Shu"—hatred for those who harm China.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The Odes declare, "Smite the Rong and Di, punish Jing and Shu"—revulsion at those who harm the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 春秋之世，楚滅陳、鄭，而卒復其祀，聖人善之。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn era, Chu destroyed Chen and Zheng yet eventually restored their sacrifices—the sage approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn period Chu destroyed Chen and Zheng yet eventually restored their ancestral rites—the sage praised this.

sentences.zh: 處存平黃巢，定京師，功冠諸將。

translations.literal: Chuzun pacified Huang Chao, secured the capital, and his merit surpassed all other generals.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun crushed Huang Chao, stabilized the capital, and his achievements surpassed those of all other generals.

sentences.zh: 昭宗嘗有意都襄陽，依趙凝以自全。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong once intended to make Xiangyang his capital and rely on Zhao Ning to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong once planned to make Xiangyang his capital and rely on Zhao Ning for safety.

sentences.zh: 大抵唐室屏翰，皆為朱溫所翦覆，過於夷狄、荊舒之為害也，甚矣。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the Tang dynasty's shield-and bulwark lords were all cut down by Zhu Quanzhong—a harm surpassing that of the barbarians and of Jing and Shu. How great it was!
translations.idiomatic: In the end, nearly all of the Tang dynasty's frontier bulwarks were destroyed by Zhu Quanzhong—a calamity greater even than that wrought by barbarians and by Jing and Shu. The ruin was profound.
